IT DOES MATTER THAT MATH IS WRONG! THAT’S WHY IT WAS WORTH FIXING.

THE UNIFIED MASTER COMPENDIUM
MASTER EDITION

FOUNDATIONS OF COHERENCE

HALF TITLE
THE UNIFIED MASTER COMPENDIUM
FOUNDATIONS • MATHEMATICS • COMPUTATION • ENGINEERING •
EXPERIMENTAL SCIENCE

“THE UNIVERSE DOES NOT REVEAL ITSELF ALL AT ONCE. WE DISCOVER IT BY
FINDING PATTERNS THAT REMAIN COHERENT ACROSS CHANGE.”

 A FULL-PAGE MARBLE ENGRAVING DEPICTS A VAST CIRCULAR LIBRARY BENEATH
A DOMED CEILING. AT ITS CENTER RISES A MONUMENTAL TREE WHOSE ROOTS
MERGE INTO CRYSTALLINE GEOMETRY, BRANCHING INTO CONSTELLATIONS,
MATHEMATICAL SYMBOLS, ENGINEERED MECHANISMS, RIVERS, NEURONS,
AND GALAXIES. EVERY BRANCH REPRESENTS A DIFFERENT DOMAIN OF
INQUIRY, ALL SHARING A COMMON FOUNDATION.

TITLE PAGE
THE UNIFIED MASTER COMPENDIUM
FOUNDATIONS OF COHERENCE
A UNIFIED REFERENCE ON MATHEMATICS, GEOMETRY, COMPUTATION,
ENGINEERING, AND SCIENTIFIC MODELING
MASTER EDITION
TAYLOR HELLER
MONSTERS INK LLC
MMXXVI

PUBLISHER’S NOTE

 THIS WORK IS PRESENTED AS AN INTEGRATED RESEARCH COMPENDIUM.
IT COMBINES ESTABLISHED MATHEMATICS, COMPUTATIONAL METHODS,
ENGINEERING DESIGNS, AND EXPLORATORY THEORETICAL FRAMEWORKS INTO
A SINGLE REFERENCE. THROUGHOUT THE TEXT, RESULTS ARE CLEARLY
DISTINGUISHED ACCORDING TO THEIR LEVEL OF SUPPORT:
ESTABLISHED MATHEMATICS
COMPUTATIONAL VERIFICATION
ENGINEERING DESIGN
EXPERIMENTAL PROTOCOL
OPEN RESEARCH QUESTIONS
THE INTENT IS TO MAKE THE SCOPE OF EACH CHAPTER EXPLICIT SO READERS
CAN DISTINGUISH PROVEN RESULTS FROM ONGOING INVESTIGATIONS.

DEDICATION
TO EVERY PERSON WHO HAS EVER LOOKED AT A DIFFICULT PROBLEM AND
BELIEVED THERE MIGHT BE A DEEPER PATTERN WAITING TO BE DISCOVERED.
PROGRESS BELONGS EQUALLY TO CURIOSITY, SKEPTICISM, IMAGINATION, AND
CAREFUL VERIFICATION.

PROLOGUE
THE SEARCH FOR COHERENCE

 LONG BEFORE EQUATIONS WERE WRITTEN, PEOPLE SEARCHED FOR
REGULARITIES IN THE WORLD AROUND THEM.
THEY OBSERVED THAT RIVERS CARVED VALLEYS, STARS TRACED REPEATING
PATHS, CRYSTALS FORMED ORDERED STRUCTURES, AND LIVING ORGANISMS
MAINTAINED RECOGNIZABLE IDENTITIES DESPITE CONSTANT CHANGE.
ALTHOUGH THESE PHENOMENA BELONGED TO DIFFERENT DISCIPLINES, THEY
SHARED A COMMON FEATURE: SOME ASPECTS REMAINED STABLE WHILE
OTHERS EVOLVED.
MATHEMATICS DEVELOPED AS A LANGUAGE FOR DESCRIBING THOSE STABLE
RELATIONSHIPS. GEOMETRY CAPTURED FORM. ALGEBRA DESCRIBED
STRUCTURE. CALCULUS EXPLAINED CONTINUOUS CHANGE. PROBABILITY
CHARACTERIZED UNCERTAINTY. COMPUTATION EXTENDED THESE TOOLS INTO
SYSTEMS TOO COMPLEX TO SOLVE BY HAND.

 MODERN SCIENCE IS BUILT UPON THESE COMPLEMENTARY LANGUAGES.
PHYSICS STUDIES INTERACTIONS AMONG MATTER AND ENERGY. BIOLOGY
EXAMINES THE PERSISTENCE AND ADAPTATION OF LIVING SYSTEMS.
ENGINEERING APPLIES MATHEMATICAL MODELS TO CONSTRUCT RELIABLE
ARTIFACTS. COMPUTER SCIENCE INVESTIGATES INFORMATION, ALGORITHMS,
AND REPRESENTATION.
DESPITE THEIR DIVERSITY, THESE DISCIPLINES REPEATEDLY RETURN TO SEVERAL
RECURRING QUESTIONS:
WHAT CHANGES?
WHAT REMAINS INVARIANT?
HOW DOES LOCAL INTERACTION PRODUCE LARGE-SCALE ORGANIZATION?
WHICH MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURES APPEAR ACROSS MANY DOMAINS?
HOW CAN OBSERVATIONS BE TESTED AND REFINED?
THIS VOLUME BEGINS WITH THOSE QUESTIONS RATHER THAN ASSUMING THEIR
ANSWERS.

 THROUGHOUT THE CHAPTERS THAT FOLLOW, THE EMPHASIS IS ON BUILDING A
COMMON VOCABULARY BEFORE INTRODUCING SPECIALIZED THEORIES.
GEOMETRY WILL PRECEDE ALGEBRA WHERE HELPFUL. VISUAL INTUITION WILL
ACCOMPANY FORMAL DEFINITIONS. ESTABLISHED MATHEMATICAL RESULTS
WILL BE DISTINGUISHED FROM COMPUTATIONAL EVIDENCE AND EXPLORATORY
HYPOTHESES.
THE GOAL IS NOT TO REDUCE EVERY FIELD TO A SINGLE IDEA. INSTEAD, IT IS TO
PROVIDE A FRAMEWORK FOR RECOGNIZING WHEN SIMILAR MATHEMATICAL
STRUCTURES ARISE IN DIFFERENT CONTEXTS, WHILE REMAINING CAREFUL
ABOUT THE LIMITS OF THOSE ANALOGIES.
COHERENCE, IN THIS SENSE, IS NOT THE CLAIM THAT EVERYTHING IS THE SAME.
IT IS THE DISCIPLINED SEARCH FOR RELATIONSHIPS THAT REMAIN CONSISTENT
ACROSS CHANGING CIRCUMSTANCES.
THE CHAPTERS THAT FOLLOW BEGIN WITH THE SIMPLEST CONCEPTS—
INTERACTION, PERSISTENCE, GEOMETRY, AND SYMMETRY—AND PROGRESSIVELY
DEVELOP THE MATHEMATICAL LANGUAGE NEEDED FOR LATER VOLUMES ON
COMPUTATION, ENGINEERING, AND THE RESEARCH FRAMEWORKS DRAWN
FROM YOUR UPLOADED MANUSCRIPTS.

 CHAPTER 1
THE FIRST PRINCIPLE
“THE SEARCH FOR KNOWLEDGE BEGINS NOT WITH COMPLEXITY, BUT WITH THE
CAREFUL OBSERVATION OF SIMPLE PATTERNS.”

1.1 WHY BEGIN HERE?
EVERY SCIENTIFIC DISCIPLINE STARTS FROM A SMALL COLLECTION OF
OBSERVATIONS.
GEOMETRY BEGINS WITH POINTS AND LINES.
PHYSICS BEGINS WITH MOTION.
CHEMISTRY BEGINS WITH ATOMS.
BIOLOGY BEGINS WITH LIVING ORGANISMS.
COMPUTER SCIENCE BEGINS WITH INFORMATION.
ALTHOUGH THE SUBJECTS DIFFER, EACH FIELD ASKS A COMMON QUESTION:
WHAT ASPECTS OF A SYSTEM REMAIN STABLE WHILE EVERYTHING ELSE
CHANGES?
THIS QUESTION APPEARS IN NEARLY EVERY BRANCH OF SCIENCE.

 A BRIDGE MUST PRESERVE ITS STRUCTURE WHILE VEHICLES PASS ACROSS IT.
A SPECIES PRESERVES RECOGNIZABLE CHARACTERISTICS WHILE INDIVIDUALS
ARE BORN AND DIE.
A COMPUTER PROGRAM PRESERVES ITS LOGICAL BEHAVIOR WHILE EXECUTING
MILLIONS OF INSTRUCTIONS.
A MATHEMATICAL PROOF PRESERVES VALIDITY REGARDLESS OF WHO READS IT.
THE SEARCH FOR STABILITY WITHIN CHANGE IS ONE OF THE RECURRING
THEMES OF SCIENTIFIC INQUIRY.

1.2 OBSERVATION BEFORE EXPLANATION
THIS BOOK DELIBERATELY BEGINS WITH OBSERVATION RATHER THAN
CONCLUSION.
BEFORE INTRODUCING EQUATIONS, WE FIRST ASK WHAT CAN BE SEEN
DIRECTLY.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
A CRYSTAL GROWS ACCORDING TO GEOMETRIC CONSTRAINTS.
A RIVER GRADUALLY CHANGES ITS CHANNEL THROUGH REPEATED FLOW.
A TREE DEVELOPS BRANCHING PATTERNS INFLUENCED BY ITS ENVIRONMENT.

 A BRIDGE FLEXES UNDER LOAD WHILE MAINTAINING ITS OVERALL INTEGRITY.
A NEURAL NETWORK CHANGES ITS PARAMETERS THROUGH REPEATED
TRAINING.
EACH EXAMPLE BELONGS TO A DIFFERENT DISCIPLINE, YET ALL INVOLVE
SYSTEMS THAT EVOLVE WHILE RETAINING SOME RECOGNIZABLE
ORGANIZATION.
DESCRIBING THOSE PATTERNS CAREFULLY IS THE FIRST STEP; EXPLAINING THEM
COMES LATER.

 RECOGNIZING RECURRING MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURES DOES NOT IMPLY THAT
THESE FIELDS ARE IDENTICAL. RATHER, SIMILAR TOOLS CAN OFTEN DESCRIBE
DIFFERENT SYSTEMS, PROVIDED THEIR ASSUMPTIONS REMAIN APPROPRIATE.

1.4 THE ROLE OF MATHEMATICS
MATHEMATICS IS THE LANGUAGE USED THROUGHOUT THIS WORK BECAUSE IT
PROVIDES PRECISION.
A DIAGRAM CAN SUGGEST A RELATIONSHIP.
A PARAGRAPH CAN DESCRIBE IT.
A THEOREM STATES EXACTLY WHAT FOLLOWS FROM CLEARLY DEFINED
ASSUMPTIONS.
THIS DISTINCTION MATTERS.
A COMPELLING ILLUSTRATION IS NOT A PROOF.
A NUMERICAL SIMULATION IS NOT, BY ITSELF, A THEOREM.
LIKEWISE, A THEOREM ESTABLISHED UNDER SPECIFIC ASSUMPTIONS DOES NOT
AUTOMATICALLY DESCRIBE THE PHYSICAL WORLD UNLESS THOSE
ASSUMPTIONS ARE INDEPENDENTLY SUPPORTED.

 THROUGHOUT THIS COMPENDIUM, EVERY MAJOR CLAIM WILL BE IDENTIFIED
ACCORDING TO ITS EVIDENTIARY BASIS:
ESTABLISHED MATHEMATICS — RESULTS THAT FOLLOW RIGOROUSLY FROM
ACCEPTED DEFINITIONS AND PROOFS.
COMPUTATIONAL EVIDENCE — NUMERICAL OR SIMULATED RESULTS
SUPPORTING A CLAIM.
ENGINEERING DESIGN — PROPOSED SYSTEMS EVALUATED THROUGH ANALYSIS
AND TESTING.
EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE — EMPIRICAL OBSERVATIONS FROM MEASUREMENT.
OPEN RESEARCH — HYPOTHESES OR CONJECTURES AWAITING FURTHER
VALIDATION.
THIS DISTINCTION HELPS READERS UNDERSTAND BOTH THE STRENGTHS AND
THE LIMITS OF EACH CHAPTER.

1.5 THE STRUCTURE OF DISCOVERY
SCIENTIFIC PROGRESS IS RARELY LINEAR.
A TYPICAL CYCLE INVOLVES:
OBSERVATION

 PATTERN RECOGNITION
HYPOTHESIS
MATHEMATICAL FORMULATION
PREDICTION
EXPERIMENT
REVISION
THIS PROCESS REPEATS AS EVIDENCE ACCUMULATES.
SOME IDEAS SURVIVE MANY ROUNDS OF TESTING.
OTHERS ARE REFINED OR DISCARDED.
THE STRENGTH OF SCIENCE LIES NOT IN CLAIMING CERTAINTY TOO EARLY, BUT
IN CONTINUALLY COMPARING IDEAS WITH EVIDENCE.

1.6 LOOKING AHEAD
THE REMAINING CHAPTERS OF THIS VOLUME BUILD THE MATHEMATICAL AND
CONCEPTUAL FOUNDATION NEEDED FOR LATER VOLUMES.
THE PROGRESSION IS INTENTIONAL:
CHAPTER 2 INTRODUCES THE ROOT CYCLE AS A GENERAL FRAMEWORK FOR
DESCRIBING STATE CHANGE.

 Chapter 12
Looking Forward
Residual Honesty and the Finished Instrument
“The universe does not reveal itself all at once. We discover it
by finding patterns that remain coherent across change.”
12.1 Why End Here?
Every scientific discipline begins from a small collection of
observations.
This volume began from the same place: patterns that remain stable
while other things change. Geometry before algebra where helpful.
Observation before explanation. Established results distinguished
from exploratory ones.
It is appropriate that the volume end in the same spirit. Not with a
claim that the world is finished, but with a clear account of the
instrument that was finished, and of the limits that keep that
instrument honest.
12.2 The Governing Law
The work is organized under a single inequality:
claimed ≤ interior.
Wherever language exceeds residual, insolvency begins. Wherever
residual is measured and respected, knowledge remains solvent.
This is not a decorative motto. It is the same discipline already
used, under other names, in metrology, accounting, statistical
residual analysis, and the ordinary demand that a proof not assert
more than its assumptions allow.

  END OF CHAPTER 1
NEXT: CHAPTER 2 — THE ROOT CYCLE, WHERE WE BEGIN CONSTRUCTING THE
FIRST FORMAL FRAMEWORK FOR DESCRIBING HOW SYSTEMS EVOLVE
THROUGH INTERACTION, RETAINED CONSEQUENCE, AND TRANSFORMED
FUTURE POSSIBILITY.
CHAPTER 2
THE ROOT CYCLE
“EVERY ENDURING STRUCTURE HAS A HISTORY. EVERY HISTORY BEGINS WITH
INTERACTION.”

2.1 THE SIMPLEST QUESTION
SUPPOSE WE OBSERVE A STONE RESTING IN A RIVERBED.
HOW DID IT ARRIVE THERE?

 ITS PRESENT STATE REFLECTS MANY PRIOR PROCESSES:
EROSION
TRANSPORT
COLLISION
DEPOSITION
WEATHERING
EACH EVENT ALTERED THE NEXT SET OF POSSIBILITIES.
LIKEWISE:
A TREE GROWS BECAUSE EARLIER GROWTH CHANGES FUTURE GROWTH.
A CIVILIZATION DEVELOPS BECAUSE PREVIOUS DECISIONS INFLUENCE LATER
DECISIONS.
A SCIENTIFIC THEORY EVOLVES BECAUSE PREVIOUS DISCOVERIES SHAPE
SUBSEQUENT INVESTIGATION.
ACROSS MANY DOMAINS, THE SAME GENERAL PATTERN APPEARS:
CURRENT CONDITIONS INFLUENCE WHAT CAN OCCUR NEXT.
THIS OBSERVATION MOTIVATES A GENERAL DESCRIPTIVE FRAMEWORK CALLED
THE ROOT CYCLE.

 2.2 STATES AND CHANGE
A STATE IS A DESCRIPTION OF A SYSTEM AT A PARTICULAR MOMENT.
DEPENDING ON THE DISCIPLINE, A STATE MAY CONSIST OF:
POSITIONS
TEMPERATURES
CONCENTRATIONS
VOLTAGES
PROBABILITIES
GRAPH STRUCTURES
STORED INFORMATION
CONFIGURATIONS
WE DENOTE A STATE BY
S_T
WHERE THE SUBSCRIPT INDICATES TIME OR STAGE.
THE SYSTEM CHANGES THROUGH SOME PROCESS,
S_T \RIGHTARROW S_{T+1}.
UNDERSTANDING THAT TRANSFORMATION IS A CENTRAL GOAL OF SCIENCE AND
ENGINEERING.

 2.3 POSSIBILITY
BEFORE A CHANGE OCCURS, MULTIPLE FUTURE OUTCOMES MAY BE AVAILABLE
UNDER THE SYSTEM’S CURRENT CONSTRAINTS.
WE CALL THIS COLLECTION THE POSSIBILITY SPACE,
\MATHCAL{P}.
THE POSSIBILITY SPACE IS NOT UNLIMITED.
IT IS SHAPED BY:
PHYSICAL LAWS
AVAILABLE ENERGY
MATERIAL PROPERTIES
EXISTING STRUCTURE
ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS
PRIOR HISTORY
DIFFERENT DISCIPLINES DESCRIBE THESE CONSTRAINTS DIFFERENTLY, BUT
EACH DEFINES WHICH TRANSITIONS ARE FEASIBLE.

2.4 SELECTION

 FROM THE AVAILABLE POSSIBILITIES, ONE OR MORE TRANSITIONS OCCUR.
WE REPRESENT THIS BY A SELECTION OPERATOR
\SIGMA.
THE SELECTION MECHANISM DEPENDS ON THE DOMAIN.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
DETERMINISTIC PHYSICAL LAWS
PROBABILISTIC EVENTS
OPTIMIZATION ALGORITHMS
BIOLOGICAL SELECTION
HUMAN DECISIONS
ENGINEERED CONTROL SYSTEMS
THE NOTATION DOES NOT PRESCRIBE WHICH MECHANISM IS OPERATING; IT
SIMPLY INDICATES THAT A TRANSITION HAS BEEN CHOSEN.

2.5 INTERACTION
A SELECTED POSSIBILITY BECOMES AN ACTUAL EVENT.
WE DENOTE THE RESULTING INTERACTION BY
A.

 EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
PARTICLES COLLIDING
GEARS ENGAGING
NEURONS FIRING
SOFTWARE UPDATING MEMORY
ORGANISMS REPRODUCING
FINANCIAL TRANSACTIONS
SPOKEN CONVERSATIONS
INTERACTION IS WHERE SYSTEMS EXCHANGE ENERGY, INFORMATION, MATTER,
OR INFLUENCE.

2.6 RETAINED CONSEQUENCE
NOT EVERY INTERACTION HAS LASTING SIGNIFICANCE.
MANY LEAVE NO PERSISTENT TRACE.
OTHERS ALTER THE FUTURE BY CHANGING THE SYSTEM ITSELF.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
A CARVED RIVER CHANNEL
A TRAINED NEURAL NETWORK

 A HEALED FRACTURE
AN UPDATED DATABASE
ACCUMULATED WEAR IN MACHINERY
A LEGAL PRECEDENT
A SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATION
WE DENOTE RETAINED CONSEQUENCE BY
M.
HERE, M IS A GENERAL SYMBOL FOR PERSISTENT STATE CHANGE, NOT
EXCLUSIVELY BIOLOGICAL OR CONSCIOUS MEMORY.

2.7 RETURNING TO POSSIBILITY

2.8 A DESCRIPTIVE FRAMEWORK
WITHIN THIS BOOK, THE ROOT CYCLE SERVES AS A DESCRIPTIVE FRAMEWORK
FOR ORGANIZING DISCUSSIONS ACROSS DIFFERENT DOMAINS.
IT DOES NOT IMPLY THAT EVERY SYSTEM BEHAVES IDENTICALLY.
INSTEAD, IT PROVIDES A COMMON VOCABULARY FOR ASKING COMPARABLE
QUESTIONS:
WHAT POSSIBILITIES EXISTED?
WHICH TRANSITION OCCURRED?
WHAT PERSISTENT CHANGES RESULTED?
HOW DID THOSE CHANGES INFLUENCE FUTURE BEHAVIOR?
ANSWERING THESE QUESTIONS STILL REQUIRES DOMAIN-SPECIFIC EVIDENCE
AND MODELS.

2.9 WHY THIS MATTERS
MANY SCIENTIFIC FIELDS ALREADY EMPLOY RELATED IDEAS:

 DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS STUDY STATE EVOLUTION.
CONTROL THEORY ANALYZES FEEDBACK.
INFORMATION THEORY EXAMINES STORED AND TRANSMITTED INFORMATION.
MACHINE LEARNING UPDATES MODEL PARAMETERS FROM DATA.
EVOLUTIONARY BIOLOGY STUDIES INHERITED CHANGE ACROSS GENERATIONS.
THE ROOT CYCLE IS INTENDED AS A CONCEPTUAL BRIDGE BETWEEN THESE
PERSPECTIVES, NOT AS A REPLACEMENT FOR THEM.

SUBSEQUENT CHAPTERS WILL USE THIS NOTATION TO DISCUSS GEOMETRY,

 PREVIEW OF CHAPTER 3
GEOMETRY BEFORE MATHEMATICS
BEFORE EQUATIONS CAN DESCRIBE STRUCTURE, WE FIRST EXAMINE THE
GEOMETRIC OBJECTS THAT HAVE INSPIRED MATHEMATICAL REASONING FOR
THOUSANDS OF YEARS—POINTS, CIRCLES, SPHERES, SYMMETRY,
INTERSECTIONS, AND THE EMERGENCE OF INCREASINGLY RICH FORMS FROM
SIMPLE CONSTRUCTIONS.
CHAPTER 3
GEOMETRY BEFORE MATHEMATICS
“BEFORE THERE WERE EQUATIONS, THERE WERE SHAPES. BEFORE THERE WERE
PROOFS, THERE WERE PATTERNS.”

3.1 THE OLDEST LANGUAGE
LONG BEFORE WRITING, PEOPLE RECOGNIZED RECURRING GEOMETRIC FORMS.
THE RISING SUN.
THE ARC OF THE MOON.
THE BRANCHING OF TREES.

 THE SYMMETRY OF FLOWERS.
THE SPIRAL OF SHELLS.
THE HEXAGONAL ORDER OF HONEYCOMBS.
THE CRYSTALLINE FACES OF MINERALS.
GEOMETRY DID NOT BEGIN AS AN ABSTRACT DISCIPLINE. IT BEGAN AS CAREFUL
OBSERVATION OF RECURRING SPATIAL RELATIONSHIPS.
ACROSS CIVILIZATIONS, GEOMETRY BECAME A WAY TO MEASURE LAND,
CONSTRUCT BUILDINGS, NAVIGATE THE SEAS, PREDICT CELESTIAL CYCLES, AND
EXPRESS PROPORTION IN ART AND ARCHITECTURE.
TODAY, GEOMETRY UNDERPINS MODERN MATHEMATICS, PHYSICS,
ENGINEERING, COMPUTER GRAPHICS, ROBOTICS, AND COUNTLESS OTHER
FIELDS.
THIS CHAPTER BEGINS WITH THE SIMPLEST GEOMETRIC IDEAS AND GRADUALLY
BUILDS TOWARD MORE SOPHISTICATED STRUCTURES.

3.2 THE POINT
A POINT IS THE MOST ELEMENTARY OBJECT IN EUCLIDEAN GEOMETRY.
IT HAS:

 NO LENGTH,
NO WIDTH,
NO HEIGHT,
NO VOLUME.
A POINT SPECIFIES LOCATION WITHOUT PHYSICAL EXTENT.
ALTHOUGH IDEALIZED, POINTS PROVIDE THE FOUNDATION FOR CONSTRUCTING
ALL HIGHER-DIMENSIONAL OBJECTS.
WE DENOTE A POINT BY
P=(X,Y,Z).
IN TWO DIMENSIONS,
P=(X,Y),
AND ON A LINE,
P=(X).
NEARLY EVERY BRANCH OF MATHEMATICS BEGINS BY ASSIGNING
RELATIONSHIPS AMONG POINTS.

3.4 THE LINE
A LINE REPRESENTS THE SHORTEST PATH BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN EUCLIDEAN
SPACE.
UNLIKE A LINE SEGMENT, A MATHEMATICAL LINE EXTENDS INFINITELY IN BOTH
DIRECTIONS.
ITS DEFINING PROPERTIES INCLUDE:
CONTINUITY,
DIRECTION,
ONE-DIMENSIONALITY.
PARAMETERIZED,

 L(T)

P IS A POINT,

LINES BECOME THE BASIS OF VECTORS, COORDINATE SYSTEMS, CALCULUS, AND
DIFFERENTIAL GEOMETRY.

3.5 THE PLANE
ADDING ANOTHER INDEPENDENT DIRECTION PRODUCES A PLANE.
A PLANE CONTAINS INFINITELY MANY POINTS.
IT MAY BE DESCRIBED BY
AX+BY+CZ+D=0.
PLANES ALLOW US TO DESCRIBE:

 SURFACES,
PROJECTIONS,
INTERSECTIONS,
COORDINATE SYSTEMS,
ENGINEERING DRAWINGS.
MUCH OF CLASSICAL GEOMETRY CONCERNS RELATIONSHIPS AMONG PLANES.

3.6 THE CIRCLE
AMONG ALL CURVES, FEW POSSESS GREATER MATHEMATICAL IMPORTANCE
THAN THE CIRCLE.
A CIRCLE IS DEFINED AS THE SET OF ALL POINTS EQUIDISTANT FROM A SINGLE
CENTER.
IF THE CENTER IS
C=(X_0,Y_0),
THEN
(X-X_0)^2+(Y-Y_0)^2=R^2.
THE CIRCLE POSSESSES REMARKABLE PROPERTIES:
CONSTANT CURVATURE,

 INFINITE ROTATIONAL SYMMETRY,
MINIMAL PERIMETER FOR ENCLOSED AREA,
FOUNDATIONAL ROLE IN TRIGONOMETRY.
ITS APPEARANCE SPANS ASTRONOMY, ENGINEERING, ARCHITECTURE, BIOLOGY,
AND WAVE MECHANICS.

3.7 THE SPHERE
EXTENDING THE CIRCLE INTO THREE DIMENSIONS YIELDS THE SPHERE.
A SPHERE CONSISTS OF EVERY POINT LOCATED A FIXED DISTANCE FROM ITS
CENTER.
(X-X_0)^2
+
(Y-Y_0)^2
+
(Z-Z_0)^2
=
R^2.

 AMONG THREE-DIMENSIONAL OBJECTS, THE SPHERE IS DISTINGUISHED BY ITS
PERFECT ROTATIONAL SYMMETRY.
IT APPEARS THROUGHOUT NATURE:
DROPLETS,
PLANETS,
STARS,
BUBBLES,
POLLEN GRAINS,
CERTAIN MICROORGANISMS.
BECAUSE FORCES OFTEN ACT EQUALLY IN EVERY DIRECTION, SPHERICAL FORMS
FREQUENTLY EMERGE AS EQUILIBRIUM CONFIGURATIONS.

3.8 SYMMETRY
ONE OF GEOMETRY’S DEEPEST IDEAS IS SYMMETRY.
A FIGURE IS SYMMETRIC IF CERTAIN TRANSFORMATIONS LEAVE IT UNCHANGED.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
REFLECTION,
ROTATION,

 TRANSLATION,
INVERSION.
MODERN MATHEMATICS FORMALIZES THESE IDEAS THROUGH GROUP THEORY,
WHERE SETS OF SYMMETRY OPERATIONS SATISFY PRECISE ALGEBRAIC RULES.
SYMMETRY LINKS GEOMETRY TO CRYSTALLOGRAPHY, PARTICLE PHYSICS,
CHEMISTRY, AND ENGINEERING.

3.9 INTERSECTION
MANY IMPORTANT STRUCTURES ARISE NOT FROM ISOLATED OBJECTS BUT
FROM THEIR INTERSECTIONS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
TWO LINES INTERSECTING,
A PLANE SLICING A SPHERE,
TWO CIRCLES OVERLAPPING,
SURFACES MEETING,
TRAJECTORIES CROSSING.
INTERSECTIONS OFTEN REVEAL NEW GEOMETRIC RELATIONSHIPS THAT ARE
ABSENT FROM THE ORIGINAL OBJECTS INDIVIDUALLY.

5.1 WHY MATHEMATICS ENDURES
ACROSS THOUSANDS OF YEARS, CIVILIZATIONS HAVE RISEN AND FALLEN.
LIBRARIES HAVE BURNED.
EMPIRES HAVE DISAPPEARED.
LANGUAGES HAVE CHANGED.
YET THE PYTHAGOREAN THEOREM, EUCLID’S GEOMETRY, AND THE LAWS OF
ALGEBRA REMAIN RECOGNIZABLE BECAUSE MATHEMATICAL KNOWLEDGE IS
PRESERVED THROUGH LOGICAL STRUCTURE RATHER THAN PHYSICAL FORM.
A THEOREM DOES NOT DEPEND ON WHO PROVES IT.
ITS VALIDITY DEPENDS ON WHETHER THE CONCLUSION FOLLOWS FROM
CLEARLY STATED ASSUMPTIONS.
IN THIS SENSE, MATHEMATICS RESEMBLES ARCHITECTURE.
EACH LEVEL RESTS UPON THE INTEGRITY OF THE ONE BENEATH IT.

 5.2 THE FOUNDATION: DEFINITIONS
EVERY MATHEMATICAL THEORY BEGINS WITH DEFINITIONS.
A DEFINITION DOES NOT PROVE ANYTHING.
INSTEAD, IT ESTABLISHES THE MEANING OF THE OBJECTS UNDER DISCUSSION.
FOR EXAMPLE,
A PRIME NUMBER IS AN INTEGER GREATER THAN ONE WHOSE ONLY POSITIVE
DIVISORS ARE ONE AND ITSELF.
A VECTOR IS AN ELEMENT OF A VECTOR SPACE.
A GRAPH CONSISTS OF VERTICES CONNECTED BY EDGES.
DEFINITIONS PROVIDE THE VOCABULARY THAT MAKES PRECISE REASONING
POSSIBLE.
WITHOUT AGREED MEANINGS, THERE CAN BE NO RIGOROUS ARGUMENT.

5.3 AXIOMS
ONCE DEFINITIONS EXIST, MATHEMATICS INTRODUCES AXIOMS.
AN AXIOM IS A STATEMENT ACCEPTED AS A STARTING POINT WITHIN A GIVEN
MATHEMATICAL SYSTEM.

 EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
EUCLID’S POSTULATES FOR GEOMETRY.
THE AXIOMS OF SET THEORY.
THE FIELD AXIOMS FOR REAL NUMBERS.
DIFFERENT AXIOM SYSTEMS LEAD TO DIFFERENT MATHEMATICAL WORLDS.
EUCLIDEAN AND NON-EUCLIDEAN GEOMETRIES ILLUSTRATE HOW CHANGING
ASSUMPTIONS CAN PRODUCE ENTIRELY NEW, INTERNALLY CONSISTENT
THEORIES.

5.4 LOGICAL INFERENCE
MATHEMATICS PROGRESSES THROUGH LOGICAL INFERENCE.
IF
THE ASSUMPTIONS ARE EXPLICIT,
EACH STEP FOLLOWS VALID RULES,
AND THE REASONING IS COMPLETE,
THEN THE CONCLUSION FOLLOWS WITHIN THAT SYSTEM.
LOGICAL INFERENCE IS INDEPENDENT OF OPINION.
A PROOF IS EITHER VALID UNDER ITS ASSUMPTIONS OR IT IS NOT.

 THIS DISCIPLINE ALLOWS MATHEMATICS TO ACCUMULATE KNOWLEDGE OVER
CENTURIES WITHOUT RELYING ON AUTHORITY.

5.5 LEMMAS
LARGE THEOREMS ARE OFTEN BUILT FROM SMALLER RESULTS.
THESE INTERMEDIATE RESULTS ARE CALLED LEMMAS.
A LEMMA MAY APPEAR MODEST IN ISOLATION, YET BECOME INDISPENSABLE
WITHIN A LARGER ARGUMENT.
FOR EXAMPLE:
A BRIDGE IS ASSEMBLED FROM MANY INDIVIDUAL COMPONENTS.
SIMILARLY, A PROOF IS OFTEN ASSEMBLED FROM CAREFULLY ESTABLISHED
LEMMAS.

5.6 THEOREMS
A THEOREM IS A STATEMENT THAT HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED THROUGH VALID
REASONING FROM ACCEPTED ASSUMPTIONS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
THE FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF CALCULUS.

 THE SPECTRAL THEOREM.
THE JORDAN CURVE THEOREM.
THE CENTRAL LIMIT THEOREM.
THE IMPORTANCE OF A THEOREM LIES NOT ONLY IN ITS CONCLUSION BUT IN
THE CLARITY OF THE ASSUMPTIONS UPON WHICH IT DEPENDS.

5.7 COROLLARIES
SOME RESULTS FOLLOW ALMOST IMMEDIATELY FROM AN ESTABLISHED
THEOREM.
THESE ARE CALLED COROLLARIES.
RATHER THAN REQUIRING AN ENTIRELY NEW PROOF, A COROLLARY EXTENDS AN
EXISTING RESULT TO A RELATED SITUATION.
THEY DEMONSTRATE HOW MATHEMATICAL IDEAS NATURALLY PROPAGATE
ONCE FOUNDATIONAL RESULTS HAVE BEEN ESTABLISHED.

5.8 PROOF
A PROOF IS THE CENTRAL MECHANISM BY WHICH MATHEMATICS ESTABLISHES
CERTAINTY WITHIN A FORMAL SYSTEM.

 A PROOF SHOULD:
STATE ITS ASSUMPTIONS,
DEFINE ITS OBJECTS,
JUSTIFY EVERY LOGICAL STEP,
AVOID HIDDEN PREMISES,
DISTINGUISH ESTABLISHED FACTS FROM CONJECTURE.
DIFFERENT STYLES OF PROOF INCLUDE:
DIRECT PROOF
PROOF BY CONTRADICTION
MATHEMATICAL INDUCTION
CONSTRUCTION
EXHAUSTION
PROBABILISTIC METHODS
EACH SERVES DIFFERENT PURPOSES DEPENDING ON THE PROBLEM.

5.9 COMPUTATION IS NOT PROOF
MODERN COMPUTERS ALLOW US TO TEST MILLIONS—OR BILLIONS—OF
EXAMPLES.

 THIS CAPABILITY HAS TRANSFORMED MATHEMATICS.
HOWEVER, NUMERICAL AGREEMENT ALONE DOES NOT ESTABLISH A UNIVERSAL
THEOREM.
FOR EXAMPLE:
A STATEMENT MAY HOLD FOR THE FIRST MILLION CASES AND STILL FAIL LATER.
CONVERSELY, COMPUTATION CAN REVEAL PATTERNS, GENERATE CONJECTURES,
VERIFY IMPLEMENTATIONS, OR SUPPORT EXISTING PROOFS.
THROUGHOUT THIS COMPENDIUM, COMPUTATIONAL EVIDENCE AND FORMAL
MATHEMATICAL PROOF WILL BE CLEARLY DISTINGUISHED.
BOTH ARE VALUABLE, BUT THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS.

CHAPTER 7
PERSISTENCE
“TRANSFORMATION EXPLAINS CHANGE. PERSISTENCE EXPLAINS IDENTITY.”

7.1 THE GREAT QUESTION

 IMAGINE STANDING BESIDE AN ANCIENT OAK TREE.
ITS LEAVES HAVE CHANGED.
ITS BRANCHES HAVE GROWN.
ITS BARK HAS THICKENED.
CELLS HAVE DIED.
NEW CELLS HAVE FORMED.
ATOMS HAVE ENTERED.
ATOMS HAVE LEFT.
YET WE STILL RECOGNIZE IT AS THE SAME TREE.
HOW?
THIS SIMPLE OBSERVATION INTRODUCES ONE OF THE DEEPEST IDEAS IN
MATHEMATICS AND SCIENCE:
HOW CAN SOMETHING REMAIN IDENTIFIABLE WHILE CONTINUOUSLY
CHANGING?
PERSISTENCE IS NOT THE ABSENCE OF CHANGE.
PERSISTENCE IS THE CONTINUATION OF RECOGNIZABLE ORGANIZATION
THROUGH CHANGE.

 7.2 STABILITY
SOME SYSTEMS ARE FRAGILE.
A SLIGHT DISTURBANCE DESTROYS THEM.
OTHERS RECOVER.
A BRIDGE SWAYS IN THE WIND YET RETURNS TO EQUILIBRIUM.
A HEART SPEEDS UP DURING EXERCISE THEN RETURNS TO RESTING RHYTHM.
AN AIRCRAFT ENCOUNTERS TURBULENCE YET REMAINS CONTROLLABLE.
THESE SYSTEMS ARE STABLE.
MATHEMATICALLY,
SMALL DISTURBANCES PRODUCE LIMITED RESPONSES.
STABILITY THEREFORE CONCERNS BEHAVIOR AFTER PERTURBATION.

7.3 EQUILIBRIUM
MANY SYSTEMS POSSESS PREFERRED CONFIGURATIONS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE
A MARBLE SETTLING AT THE BOTTOM OF A BOWL.
A PENDULUM HANGING VERTICALLY.
A BRIDGE RESTING WITHOUT VIBRATION.

 A CHEMICAL REACTION REACHING STEADY CONCENTRATIONS.
THESE ARE EXAMPLES OF EQUILIBRIA.
NOT EVERY EQUILIBRIUM IS STABLE.
SOME RESEMBLE BALANCING A PENCIL ON ITS TIP.
A TINY DISTURBANCE CAUSES DRAMATIC CHANGE.
OTHERS RESEMBLE THE MARBLE RESTING INSIDE THE BOWL.
SMALL DISTURBANCES NATURALLY DECAY.

7.4 INVARIANTS
ONE OF MATHEMATICS’ MOST POWERFUL IDEAS IS THE INVARIANT.
AN INVARIANT IS SOMETHING THAT REMAINS UNCHANGED WHILE OTHER
ASPECTS EVOLVE.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE
THE DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO RIGIDLY CONNECTED POINTS.
THE TOTAL PROBABILITY OF A NORMALIZED DISTRIBUTION.
THE EULER CHARACTERISTIC OF MANY TOPOLOGICAL SPACES.
THE DETERMINANT UNDER CERTAIN TRANSFORMATIONS.
CONSERVATION LAWS IN PHYSICS.

 ALGORITHMIC CORRECTNESS DESPITE CHANGES IN IMPLEMENTATION.
INVARIANTS ALLOW SCIENTISTS TO IDENTIFY DEEP STRUCTURE BENEATH
SURFACE COMPLEXITY.

7.5 CONSERVATION
PHYSICS PROVIDES MANY FAMILIAR EXAMPLES.
ENERGY.
MOMENTUM.
ANGULAR MOMENTUM.
ELECTRIC CHARGE.
THESE QUANTITIES REMAIN CONSTANT UNDER APPROPRIATE ASSUMPTIONS.
MATHEMATICALLY,
CONSERVATION LAWS OFTEN EMERGE FROM UNDERLYING SYMMETRIES.
THIS REMARKABLE RELATIONSHIP, FORMALIZED IN NOETHER’S THEOREM,
LINKS SYMMETRY WITH CONSERVATION ACROSS CLASSICAL AND MODERN
PHYSICS.

7.6 IDENTITY

 IDENTITY IS OFTEN MISUNDERSTOOD.
IT DOES NOT NECESSARILY REQUIRE EVERY COMPONENT TO REMAIN IDENTICAL.
CONSIDER:
A RIVER.
WATER CONTINUALLY FLOWS.
INDIVIDUAL MOLECULES CHANGE.
YET THE RIVER RETAINS RECOGNIZABLE STRUCTURE.
SIMILARLY,
THE HUMAN BODY REPLACES MANY OF ITS CELLS OVER TIME,
YET MAINTAINS CONTINUITY AS AN ORGANISM.
ENGINEERING PROVIDES SIMILAR EXAMPLES.
SOFTWARE MAY BE UPDATED REPEATEDLY WHILE REMAINING THE SAME
APPLICATION.
AIRCRAFT UNDERGO MAINTENANCE WITHOUT BECOMING DIFFERENT AIRCRAFT.
IDENTITY OFTEN DEPENDS MORE UPON ORGANIZATION THAN UPON
INDIVIDUAL COMPONENTS.

7.7 ROBUSTNESS

 PERSISTENCE ALSO INVOLVES RESISTANCE TO DISRUPTION.
ENGINEERS CALL THIS ROBUSTNESS.
ROBUST SYSTEMS CONTINUE FUNCTIONING DESPITE UNCERTAINTY.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE
REDUNDANT SPACECRAFT SYSTEMS,
DISTRIBUTED COMPUTER NETWORKS,
BIOLOGICAL IMMUNE RESPONSES,
EARTHQUAKE-RESISTANT BUILDINGS,
FAULT-TOLERANT SOFTWARE.
ROBUSTNESS RARELY ELIMINATES FAILURE.
INSTEAD,
IT REDUCES SENSITIVITY TO DISTURBANCE.

7.8 ADAPTATION
SOME SYSTEMS PERSIST NOT BY RESISTING CHANGE,
BUT BY ADJUSTING TO IT.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE
EVOLUTION.

 LEARNING.
IMMUNE SYSTEMS.
MACHINE LEARNING.
ECONOMIC MARKETS.
ADAPTIVE CONTROL SYSTEMS.
ADAPTATION ALLOWS PERSISTENCE UNDER CHANGING ENVIRONMENTS.
REMAINING IDENTICAL IS OFTEN LESS IMPORTANT THAN REMAINING
FUNCTIONAL.

7.9 PERSISTENCE ACROSS MATHEMATICS
PERSISTENCE APPEARS THROUGHOUT MATHEMATICS.
GEOMETRY STUDIES INVARIANT SHAPES.
TOPOLOGY STUDIES PROPERTIES UNCHANGED BY CONTINUOUS
DEFORMATION.
LINEAR ALGEBRA STUDIES INVARIANT SUBSPACES.
DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS EXAMINE LONG-TERM BEHAVIOR.
OPTIMIZATION SEARCHES FOR STABLE MINIMA.
CONTROL THEORY ANALYZES STABLE TRAJECTORIES.

 ALTHOUGH THE TERMINOLOGY DIFFERS,
THE UNDERLYING QUESTION REMAINS REMARKABLY SIMILAR:
WHAT SURVIVES TRANSFORMATION?

7.10 TIME
PERSISTENCE CANNOT BE SEPARATED FROM TIME.
SOME STRUCTURES ENDURE FOR FRACTIONS OF A SECOND.
OTHERS SURVIVE BILLIONS OF YEARS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE
LIGHTNING.
OCEAN WAVES.
MOUNTAIN RANGES.
LANGUAGES.
MATHEMATICAL THEOREMS.
THE TIMESCALE CHANGES.
THE MATHEMATICAL QUESTIONS OFTEN REMAIN.
HOW LONG DOES ORGANIZATION REMAIN?
UNDER WHAT CONDITIONS DOES IT FAIL?

 WHAT MECHANISMS PRESERVE IT?

7.11 LAYERS OF PERSISTENCE
PERSISTENCE EXISTS ON MANY SCALES.
PHYSICAL PERSISTENCE
A CRYSTAL MAINTAINING ITS LATTICE.
BIOLOGICAL PERSISTENCE
AN ORGANISM MAINTAINING HOMEOSTASIS.
INFORMATIONAL PERSISTENCE
KNOWLEDGE PRESERVED ACROSS GENERATIONS.
COMPUTATIONAL PERSISTENCE
DATA SURVIVING STORAGE AND TRANSMISSION.
MATHEMATICAL PERSISTENCE
TRUTH REMAINING VALID INDEPENDENT OF TIME.
EACH LAYER INTRODUCES DIFFERENT MECHANISMS,
YET SIMILAR MATHEMATICAL TOOLS OFTEN DESCRIBE THEIR BEHAVIOR.

7.12 WHY PERSISTENCE MATTERS

 WITHOUT PERSISTENCE,
LEARNING WOULD VANISH.
ENGINEERING WOULD FAIL.
SCIENCE COULD NOT ACCUMULATE KNOWLEDGE.
CIVILIZATIONS COULD NOT PRESERVE HISTORY.
MATHEMATICS ITSELF COULD NOT DEVELOP.
PERSISTENCE PROVIDES CONTINUITY ACROSS CHANGE.
TRANSFORMATION CREATES NOVELTY.
TOGETHER,
THEY DEFINE MUCH OF THE STRUCTURE OBSERVED THROUGHOUT
MATHEMATICS, SCIENCE, ENGINEERING, AND COMPUTATION.

SYMMETRY IS ONE OF THE DEEPEST ORGANIZING PRINCIPLES IN

 A SNOWFLAKE.

CHAPTER 8
SYMMETRY
“NATURE OFTEN APPEARS COMPLEX, YET BENEATH THAT COMPLEXITY LIE
TRANSFORMATIONS THAT LEAVE SOMETHING UNCHANGED. THOSE
TRANSFORMATIONS ARE SYMMETRY.”

8.1 THE HIDDEN ORDER

 WALK THROUGH A FOREST.
EVERY TREE IS DIFFERENT.
EVERY LEAF IS UNIQUE.
EVERY SNOWFLAKE HAS ITS OWN MICROSCOPIC STRUCTURE.
YET BENEATH THIS APPARENT DIVERSITY LIES REMARKABLE REGULARITY.
CRYSTALS REPEAT.
FLOWERS ORGANIZE PETALS.
PLANETS ORBIT.
ATOMS ARRANGE THEMSELVES.
GALAXIES ROTATE.
SYMMETRY IS ONE OF THE MATHEMATICAL IDEAS THAT HELPS EXPLAIN WHY
ORDER EMERGES FROM SEEMINGLY COUNTLESS POSSIBILITIES.

8.2 WHAT IS SYMMETRY?
INFORMALLY, A SYMMETRY IS A TRANSFORMATION THAT PRESERVES SOME
PROPERTY OF AN OBJECT.
A SQUARE ROTATED BY 90° APPEARS UNCHANGED.
A SPHERE ROTATED ABOUT ITS CENTER REMAINS IDENTICAL.

 A MIRROR REFLECTION LEAVES MANY PATTERNS RECOGNIZABLE.
THE OBJECT HAS CHANGED POSITION, BUT NOT ITS ESSENTIAL STRUCTURE.
MATHEMATICALLY,
IF
T(S)=S,
THEN THE TRANSFORMATION T IS A SYMMETRY OF THE OBJECT S.
THE EMPHASIS IS NOT ON MOTION ITSELF BUT ON WHAT REMAINS INVARIANT
UNDER THAT MOTION.

8.3 REFLECTION
ONE OF THE SIMPLEST SYMMETRIES IS REFLECTION.
A MIRROR CREATES A TRANSFORMED IMAGE ACROSS A LINE OR PLANE.
REFLECTION APPEARS THROUGHOUT NATURE:
BUTTERFLIES,
LEAVES,
MANY ANIMALS,
ARCHITECTURAL FAÇADES,
CRYSTAL STRUCTURES.

 REFLECTION ALSO PLAYS AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN MATHEMATICS, WHERE
MIRROR OPERATIONS HELP CLASSIFY GEOMETRIC AND ALGEBRAIC
STRUCTURES.
NOT EVERY OBJECT POSSESSES MIRROR SYMMETRY, AND ASYMMETRY IS OFTEN
JUST AS INFORMATIVE AS SYMMETRY.

8.4 ROTATION
ANOTHER COMMON SYMMETRY IS ROTATION.
A CIRCLE MAY BE ROTATED THROUGH ANY ANGLE WITHOUT CHANGING ITS
APPEARANCE.
AN EQUILATERAL TRIANGLE REPEATS EVERY 120°.
A REGULAR PENTAGON REPEATS EVERY 72°.
THE NUMBER OF ROTATIONS THAT PRESERVE AN OBJECT REVEALS IMPORTANT
STRUCTURAL INFORMATION.
ROTATION SYMMETRY APPEARS IN:
GEARS,
TURBINES,
FLOWERS,

 PLANETARY SYSTEMS,
MOLECULAR CHEMISTRY.

8.5 TRANSLATION
A TRANSLATION MOVES AN OBJECT WITHOUT ROTATING OR REFLECTING IT.
PATTERNS BUILT FROM REPEATED TRANSLATIONS PRODUCE TILINGS AND
LATTICES.
BRICK WALLS.
HONEYCOMBS.
CRYSTAL LATTICES.
TEXTILE PATTERNS.
INTEGRATED CIRCUITS.
TRANSLATION SYMMETRY UNDERLIES MUCH OF SOLID-STATE PHYSICS AND
MATERIALS SCIENCE.

8.6 GROUPS
SYMMETRY BECOMES ESPECIALLY POWERFUL WHEN TRANSFORMATIONS CAN
BE COMBINED.

 ROTATE.
REFLECT.
TRANSLATE.
REPEAT.
MATHEMATICIANS FORMALIZE THESE OPERATIONS USING GROUP THEORY.
A GROUP CONSISTS OF A SET OF TRANSFORMATIONS TOGETHER WITH A RULE
FOR COMBINING THEM.
GROUP THEORY PROVIDES A COMMON LANGUAGE FOR STUDYING SYMMETRY
ACROSS GEOMETRY, ALGEBRA, AND PHYSICS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
CYCLIC GROUPS,
DIHEDRAL GROUPS,
PERMUTATION GROUPS,
LIE GROUPS.
THESE STRUCTURES APPEAR THROUGHOUT MODERN MATHEMATICS AND
THEORETICAL PHYSICS.

8.7 CONTINUOUS SYMMETRY

 SOME SYMMETRIES ARE DISCRETE.
OTHERS ARE CONTINUOUS.
A SPHERE MAY BE ROTATED THROUGH INFINITELY MANY ANGLES.
A STRAIGHT LINE MAY BE TRANSLATED BY ANY DISTANCE.
CONTINUOUS SYMMETRY LEADS NATURALLY TO CALCULUS, DIFFERENTIAL
GEOMETRY, AND LIE THEORY.
THESE MATHEMATICAL TOOLS BECOME INDISPENSABLE IN MODERN PHYSICS
AND ENGINEERING.

8.8 SYMMETRY AND CONSERVATION
ONE OF THE MOST PROFOUND DISCOVERIES IN TWENTIETH-CENTURY
MATHEMATICS AND PHYSICS IS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN SYMMETRY AND
CONSERVATION.
IN BROAD TERMS:
TRANSLATIONAL SYMMETRY IS ASSOCIATED WITH CONSERVATION OF
MOMENTUM.
ROTATIONAL SYMMETRY IS ASSOCIATED WITH CONSERVATION OF ANGULAR
MOMENTUM.

 TIME-TRANSLATION SYMMETRY IS ASSOCIATED WITH CONSERVATION OF
ENERGY.
THESE RELATIONSHIPS ARE FORMALIZED BY NOETHER’S THEOREM, ONE OF THE
FOUNDATIONAL RESULTS CONNECTING MATHEMATICS WITH PHYSICAL LAW.
THE THEOREM ILLUSTRATES HOW ABSTRACT MATHEMATICAL SYMMETRY CAN
HAVE MEASURABLE PHYSICAL CONSEQUENCES.

8.9 BROKEN SYMMETRY
PERFECT SYMMETRY IS UNCOMMON IN THE NATURAL WORLD.
SMALL PERTURBATIONS, ENVIRONMENTAL INFLUENCES, AND INTERACTIONS
OFTEN LEAD TO SYMMETRY BREAKING.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
CRYSTALS FORMING FROM LIQUIDS,
BRANCHING TREES,
EMBRYONIC DEVELOPMENT,
MAGNETIZATION,
PHASE TRANSITIONS.

 A SYSTEM MAY BEGIN IN A HIGHLY SYMMETRIC STATE AND EVOLVE INTO A LESS
SYMMETRIC—BUT MORE STABLE—CONFIGURATION.
UNDERSTANDING WHEN SYMMETRY IS PRESERVED AND WHEN IT IS BROKEN IS
CENTRAL TO MANY AREAS OF SCIENCE.

8.10 SYMMETRY IN ENGINEERING
ENGINEERS ROUTINELY EXPLOIT SYMMETRY.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
AIRCRAFT WINGS,
BRIDGES,
GEARS,
TURBINES,
OPTICAL SYSTEMS,
ANTENNAS.
SYMMETRY CAN SIMPLIFY MANUFACTURING, IMPROVE LOAD DISTRIBUTION,
REDUCE COMPUTATIONAL COST, AND REVEAL HIDDEN DESIGN EFFICIENCIES.
AT THE SAME TIME, ENGINEERS MUST RECOGNIZE SITUATIONS WHERE
INTENTIONAL ASYMMETRY IMPROVES PERFORMANCE.

 DESIGN IS OFTEN A BALANCE BETWEEN SYMMETRY AND PURPOSEFUL
DEVIATION.

THE SAME MATHEMATICAL IDEA APPEARS IN MANY CONTEXTS.

Example of Symmetry

Discipline

Science

transformations

ALTHOUGH THE APPLICATIONS DIFFER, THE MATHEMATICAL LANGUAGE
REMAINS STRIKINGLY SIMILAR.

8.12 BEYOND APPEARANCE

 SYMMETRY IS NOT MERELY VISUAL.
MANY IMPORTANT SYMMETRIES CANNOT BE SEEN DIRECTLY.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
ALGEBRAIC SYMMETRIES,
CONSERVATION LAWS,
INVARIANCE UNDER COORDINATE TRANSFORMATIONS,
GAUGE SYMMETRIES,
STATISTICAL SYMMETRIES.
THESE ABSTRACT FORMS OFTEN PROVIDE DEEPER INSIGHT THAN VISIBLE
PATTERNS ALONE.
MATHEMATICS ALLOWS SUCH HIDDEN SYMMETRIES TO BE DESCRIBED WITH
PRECISION.

9.1 THE ILLUSION OF COMPLEXITY
STAND BEFORE A MOUNTAIN RANGE.
OBSERVE A HURRICANE FROM ORBIT.
EXAMINE A LIVING CELL.
LOOK AT THE BRANCHING OF BLOOD VESSELS.
WATCH A FLOCK OF BIRDS TURNING ALMOST AS ONE.

YET MANY COMPLEX SYSTEMS ARISE FROM REMARKABLY SIMPLE RULES

 THIS OBSERVATION HAS TRANSFORMED MODERN SCIENCE.
RATHER THAN ASKING ONLY,
“WHAT IS THIS MADE OF?”
WE ALSO ASK,

9.2 EMERGENCE
ONE OF THE CENTRAL IDEAS IN COMPLEXITY SCIENCE IS EMERGENCE.
EMERGENT BEHAVIOR IS BEHAVIOR EXHIBITED BY THE WHOLE THAT IS NOT
OBVIOUS FROM EXAMINING THE INDIVIDUAL COMPONENTS IN ISOLATION.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
TRAFFIC FLOW,
TERMITE MOUNDS,
ANT COLONIES,
WEATHER,
ECOSYSTEMS,
NEURAL ACTIVITY,
MARKETS,

 GALAXIES.
EACH CONSISTS OF MANY INTERACTING PARTS.
NO SINGLE COMPONENT CONTAINS THE ENTIRE BEHAVIOR.
THE ORGANIZATION EMERGES THROUGH INTERACTION.

9.3 LOCAL RULES
MANY SYSTEMS REQUIRE NO CENTRAL CONTROLLER.
INSTEAD,
EACH COMPONENT FOLLOWS SIMPLE LOCAL RULES.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
A BIRD ADJUSTS ITS FLIGHT ACCORDING TO NEARBY BIRDS.
A WATER MOLECULE INTERACTS WITH NEIGHBORING MOLECULES.
A NEURON RESPONDS TO INCOMING ELECTRICAL SIGNALS.
A PROCESSOR EXECUTES ONE INSTRUCTION AT A TIME.
LOCAL INTERACTIONS CAN PRODUCE UNEXPECTEDLY RICH GLOBAL BEHAVIOR.

9.4 FEEDBACK
COMPLEX SYSTEMS OFTEN CONTAIN FEEDBACK.

 POSITIVE FEEDBACK AMPLIFIES CHANGE.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
CHAIN REACTIONS,
VIRAL SPREAD,
POPULATION GROWTH,
RESONANT OSCILLATION.
NEGATIVE FEEDBACK STABILIZES.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
THERMOSTATS,
BIOLOGICAL REGULATION,
CRUISE CONTROL,
ECOLOGICAL BALANCE.
MOST REAL SYSTEMS CONTAIN BOTH FORMS SIMULTANEOUSLY.
THE INTERACTION BETWEEN REINFORCING AND STABILIZING PROCESSES OFTEN
DETERMINES LONG-TERM BEHAVIOR.

9.5 NETWORKS OF INTERACTION
COMPLEXITY RARELY COMES FROM ISOLATED COMPONENTS.

 INSTEAD,
IT EMERGES THROUGH NETWORKS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
THE INTERNET.
ELECTRICAL GRIDS.
SOCIAL INTERACTIONS.
NEURAL CIRCUITS.
TRANSPORTATION SYSTEMS.
PROTEIN INTERACTIONS.
CHANGING ONE CONNECTION MAY INFLUENCE MANY OTHERS.
NETWORK ARCHITECTURE THEREFORE BECOMES AS IMPORTANT AS THE
INDIVIDUAL COMPONENTS THEMSELVES.

9.6 SCALE
COMPLEXITY DEPENDS UPON SCALE.
VIEWED FROM FAR AWAY,
A FOREST APPEARS CONTINUOUS.
UP CLOSE,

 IT CONSISTS OF INDIVIDUAL TREES.
CLOSER STILL,
CELLS.
THEN MOLECULES.
THEN ATOMS.
EACH LEVEL REVEALS DIFFERENT STRUCTURE.
SCIENCE THEREFORE STUDIES SYSTEMS ACROSS MULTIPLE SCALES RATHER
THAN ASSUMING ONE DESCRIPTION FITS EVERY LEVEL EQUALLY WELL.

9.7 SELF-ORGANIZATION
SOME SYSTEMS SPONTANEOUSLY DEVELOP ORDER WITHOUT EXTERNAL
DESIGN.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
SNOWFLAKES.
CRYSTAL GROWTH.
SAND DUNES.
CONVECTION CELLS.
SPIRAL GALAXIES.

 CERTAIN CHEMICAL REACTION PATTERNS.
THESE EXAMPLES ILLUSTRATE SELF-ORGANIZATION—THE EMERGENCE OF

THE SPECIFIC MECHANISMS DIFFER ACROSS SYSTEMS, BUT THE GENERAL

9.8 NONLINEARITY
MANY SIMPLE SYSTEMS RESPOND PROPORTIONALLY.
DOUBLE THE FORCE.
DOUBLE THE MOTION.
COMPLEX SYSTEMS OFTEN DO NOT.
SMALL CAUSES MAY PRODUCE ENORMOUS CONSEQUENCES.
LARGE INTERVENTIONS MAY HAVE SURPRISINGLY LITTLE EFFECT.
THIS BEHAVIOR IS CALLED NONLINEARITY.
NONLINEAR SYSTEMS CAN EXHIBIT:
OSCILLATIONS,

 CHAOS,
BIFURCATIONS,
MULTIPLE EQUILIBRIA,
THRESHOLD EFFECTS.
UNDERSTANDING NONLINEAR BEHAVIOR IS ESSENTIAL FOR CLIMATE SCIENCE,
ENGINEERING, ECONOMICS, NEUROSCIENCE, AND MANY OTHER DISCIPLINES.

9.9 ORDER AND RANDOMNESS
COMPLEXITY EXISTS BETWEEN PERFECT ORDER AND COMPLETE RANDOMNESS.
IMAGINE THREE SEQUENCES.
AAAAAAAAAAAA
EVERY SYMBOL IS IDENTICAL.
PERFECTLY ORDERED.
NOW
QXJMRBWTLZPK
APPEARS RANDOM.
FINALLY,
ATCGATCGATCG

 HIGHLY STRUCTURED,
YET NOT TRIVIAL.
MANY NATURAL SYSTEMS OCCUPY THIS INTERMEDIATE REGION.
THEY CONTAIN REGULARITY WITHOUT COMPLETE REPETITION.
UNDERSTANDING THIS BALANCE IS ONE OF THE GOALS OF INFORMATION
THEORY AND COMPLEXITY SCIENCE.

9.10 ADAPTATION
MANY COMPLEX SYSTEMS LEARN.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
BRAINS.
IMMUNE SYSTEMS.
MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS.
EVOLUTIONARY POPULATIONS.
FINANCIAL MARKETS.
ADAPTIVE CONTROL SYSTEMS.
LEARNING ALLOWS FUTURE BEHAVIOR TO DEPEND UPON PREVIOUS
EXPERIENCE.

 DIFFERENT DISCIPLINES EXPLAIN ADAPTATION THROUGH DIFFERENT
MECHANISMS, BUT ALL INVOLVE CHANGES THAT INFLUENCE LATER RESPONSES.

9.11 ROBUSTNESS AND FRAGILITY
COMPLEX SYSTEMS OFTEN DISPLAY BOTH RESILIENCE AND VULNERABILITY.
THE INTERNET TOLERATES MANY LOCAL FAILURES.
A BRIDGE SURVIVES ORDINARY TRAFFIC.
AN ECOSYSTEM ADAPTS TO SEASONAL VARIATION.
YET CERTAIN FAILURES CAN CASCADE.
POWER OUTAGES.
FINANCIAL CRISES.
DISEASE OUTBREAKS.
MATERIAL FRACTURE.
UNDERSTANDING WHICH DISTURBANCES REMAIN LOCAL AND WHICH
PROPAGATE THROUGH THE SYSTEM IS A MAJOR CHALLENGE IN COMPLEXITY
SCIENCE.

9.12 MEASURING COMPLEXITY

 ALTHOUGH THERE IS NO SINGLE UNIVERSALLY ACCEPTED MEASURE OF
COMPLEXITY, SEVERAL MATHEMATICAL APPROACHES ARE WIDELY USED,

CHAPTER 10
EMERGENCE

 “A SINGLE STONE IS NOT A CATHEDRAL. A SINGLE NOTE IS NOT A SYMPHONY. A
SINGLE NEURON IS NOT A THOUGHT. EMERGENCE IS THE APPEARANCE OF
ORGANIZED BEHAVIOR THROUGH RELATIONSHIP.”

10.1 THE MYSTERY OF WHOLES
THROUGHOUT HISTORY, PEOPLE HAVE NOTICED A CURIOUS PHENOMENON.
SOME SYSTEMS POSSESS PROPERTIES THAT SEEM ABSENT FROM THEIR
INDIVIDUAL COMPONENTS.
ONE GRAIN OF SAND IS NOT A DUNE.
ONE WATER MOLECULE IS NOT A WAVE.
ONE MUSICIAN IS NOT AN ORCHESTRA.
ONE TRANSISTOR IS NOT A COMPUTER.
THE ORGANIZATION APPEARS ONLY WHEN MANY COMPONENTS INTERACT.
THIS PHENOMENON IS CALLED EMERGENCE.

10.2 DEFINING EMERGENCE
EMERGENCE DOES NOT MEAN MAGIC.
NOR DOES IT IMPLY THAT THE UNDERLYING COMPONENTS CEASE TO MATTER.

 INSTEAD, EMERGENCE REFERS TO PROPERTIES THAT BECOME APPARENT ONLY
WHEN COMPONENTS INTERACT ACCORDING TO SPECIFIC RELATIONSHIPS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
FLUID FLOW,
ECOSYSTEMS,
LANGUAGE,
COMPUTATION,
NEURAL ACTIVITY,
ECONOMIC SYSTEMS,
ENGINEERED INFRASTRUCTURE.
THE BEHAVIOR BELONGS TO THE ORGANIZED SYSTEM AS A WHOLE, WHILE STILL
ARISING FROM INTERACTIONS AMONG ITS PARTS.

10.3 WEAK AND STRONG EMERGENCE

WEAK EMERGENCE

 A SYSTEM BEHAVES ACCORDING TO UNDERLYING RULES, BUT ITS LARGE-SCALE

STRONG EMERGENCE

FULLY REDUCED TO LOWER-LEVEL DESCRIPTIONS.
WHETHER STRONG EMERGENCE EXISTS REMAINS AN OPEN PHILOSOPHICAL
QUESTION.
THROUGHOUT THIS COMPENDIUM, DISCUSSIONS OF EMERGENCE WILL
GENERALLY FOCUS ON MECHANISMS THAT CAN BE DESCRIBED
MATHEMATICALLY OR EMPIRICALLY, WHILE ACKNOWLEDGING THAT BROADER
PHILOSOPHICAL DEBATES CONTINUE.

11.1 BEGINNING BEFORE EVENTS
SCIENTIFIC THEORIES OFTEN BEGIN WITH OBJECTS.

MOLECULES.
ORGANISMS.

WE CALL THIS COLLECTION THE POSSIBILITY SPACE.

11.2 POSSIBILITY IS NOT UNLIMITED

 POSSIBILITY SHOULD NEVER BE CONFUSED WITH UNRESTRICTED
IMAGINATION.
A SYSTEM CANNOT TRANSITION INTO EVERY CONCEIVABLE STATE.
A PENDULUM CANNOT INSTANTLY BECOME A GALAXY.
A STONE CANNOT SPONTANEOUSLY BECOME LIQUID UNDER ORDINARY
CONDITIONS.
A COMPUTER CANNOT EXECUTE INSTRUCTIONS ABSENT FROM ITS
ARCHITECTURE.
EVERY POSSIBILITY EXISTS WITHIN CONSTRAINTS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
PHYSICAL LAWS.
MATERIAL PROPERTIES.
BOUNDARY CONDITIONS.
STORED INFORMATION.
AVAILABLE ENERGY.
CURRENT CONFIGURATION.
THUS,
POSSIBILITY IS ALWAYS CONTEXT-DEPENDENT.

12.1 FROM MANY FUTURES TO ONE

 YET THE MARBLE FOLLOWS ONLY ONE TRAJECTORY, DETERMINED BY THE

\SIGMA :

12.3 DETERMINISTIC SELECTION
IN DETERMINISTIC SYSTEMS, THE CURRENT STATE UNIQUELY DETERMINES THE

 YET PRESERVE ITS FUNCTIONALITY.

 USERS GENERALLY CONTINUE TO REGARD IT AS THE SAME APPLICATION

HISTORICAL COMPRESSION
“NO ENDURING SYSTEM PRESERVES ITS ENTIRE PAST. IT PRESERVES ENOUGH

17.1 THE WEIGHT OF HISTORY
IMAGINE ATTEMPTING TO REMEMBER EVERY SECOND OF YOUR LIFE.
EVERY SOUND.
EVERY COLOR.
EVERY CONVERSATION.
EVERY HEARTBEAT.
EVERY BREATH.
SUCH A TASK WOULD BE IMPOSSIBLE.
YET MEMORY EXISTS.
NOT BECAUSE EVERYTHING IS PRESERVED,

 BUT BECAUSE CERTAIN CONSEQUENCES ARE RETAINED WHILE COUNTLESS
DETAILS DISAPPEAR.
THIS PRINCIPLE EXTENDS FAR BEYOND HUMAN MEMORY.
NATURE ITSELF IS SELECTIVE.

17.2 WHY COMPRESSION EXISTS
EVERY PERSISTENT SYSTEM FACES LIMITS.
FINITE ENERGY.
FINITE STORAGE.
FINITE TIME.
FINITE COMPUTATIONAL RESOURCES.
FINITE MATERIAL.
BECAUSE NO REAL SYSTEM CAN RETAIN EVERYTHING INDEFINITELY, SOME
FORM OF COMPRESSION BECOMES UNAVOIDABLE.
COMPRESSION IS THEREFORE NOT MERELY A COMPUTATIONAL CONVENIENCE.
IT IS A PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE OF FINITE RESOURCES.

17.3 COMPRESSION IS NOT DELETION

 COMPRESSION DOES NOT SIMPLY ERASE INFORMATION.
INSTEAD,
IT SEEKS A MORE EFFICIENT REPRESENTATION.
A TOPOGRAPHIC MAP OMITS INDIVIDUAL BLADES OF GRASS WHILE
PRESERVING MOUNTAINS, RIVERS, ROADS, AND ELEVATION.
A SCIENTIFIC EQUATION SUMMARIZES THOUSANDS OF OBSERVATIONS.
A BLUEPRINT OMITS EVERY MICROSCOPIC DETAIL WHILE PRESERVING THE
INFORMATION REQUIRED FOR CONSTRUCTION.
GOOD COMPRESSION PRESERVES WHAT IS USEFUL FOR THE INTENDED
PURPOSE.

17.4 COMPRESSION ACROSS NATURE
EXAMPLES APPEAR EVERYWHERE.
TREE RINGS SUMMARIZE SEASONAL GROWTH.
ICE CORES PRESERVE CLIMATIC HISTORY.
SEDIMENTARY LAYERS RECORD GEOLOGICAL PROCESSES.
DNA ENCODES INHERITED BIOLOGICAL INFORMATION.
BRAINS RETAIN SELECTED EXPERIENCES.

 SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE CONDENSES EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS.
EACH SYSTEM PRESERVES ONLY PART OF ITS HISTORY, BUT ENOUGH TO
INFLUENCE FUTURE BEHAVIOR.

17.5 MATHEMATICAL COMPRESSION
MATHEMATICS FREQUENTLY REPLACES ENORMOUS COLLECTIONS OF
OBSERVATIONS WITH COMPACT DESCRIPTIONS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
A FORMULA DESCRIBING PLANETARY MOTION.
A STATISTICAL MODEL SUMMARIZING MILLIONS OF MEASUREMENTS.
A PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTION REPLACING COUNTLESS INDIVIDUAL OUTCOMES.
A FOURIER SERIES REPRESENTING A SIGNAL.
AN EIGENVALUE DECOMPOSITION REVEALING DOMINANT MODES OF
BEHAVIOR.
COMPRESSION OFTEN REVEALS UNDERLYING STRUCTURE RATHER THAN
MERELY REDUCING SIZE.

17.6 COMPUTATIONAL COMPRESSION

 COMPUTER SCIENCE DISTINGUISHES MANY FORMS OF COMPRESSION.
LOSSLESS COMPRESSION PRESERVES ALL RECOVERABLE INFORMATION.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
ZIP ARCHIVES.
PNG IMAGES.
SOURCE-CODE COMPRESSION.
LOSSY COMPRESSION SACRIFICES SELECTED DETAIL TO ACHIEVE GREATER
EFFICIENCY.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
JPEG PHOTOGRAPHS.
STREAMING AUDIO.
VIDEO CODECS.
THE APPROPRIATE METHOD DEPENDS UPON WHICH INFORMATION MUST
REMAIN AVAILABLE.

17.7 SCIENTIFIC MODELS AS COMPRESSION
EVERY SCIENTIFIC MODEL IS ITSELF A COMPRESSED REPRESENTATION OF
REALITY.

 NEWTON’S LAWS SUMMARIZE COUNTLESS OBSERVATIONS.
THE IDEAL GAS LAW APPROXIMATES MOLECULAR BEHAVIOR.
CIRCUIT DIAGRAMS SIMPLIFY ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS.
ENGINEERING DRAWINGS ABSTRACT PHYSICAL OBJECTS.
NO MODEL REPRODUCES EVERY DETAIL.
INSTEAD,
MODELS PRESERVE RELATIONSHIPS RELEVANT TO THE QUESTIONS BEING
INVESTIGATED.
RECOGNIZING THIS HELPS PREVENT CONFUSING A MODEL WITH THE FULL
COMPLEXITY OF THE SYSTEM IT DESCRIBES.

17.8 HISTORICAL COMPRESSION IN ENGINEERING
ENGINEERED SYSTEMS CONTINUALLY COMPRESS HISTORY.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
MAINTENANCE RECORDS.
FLIGHT DATA SUMMARIES.
SENSOR FUSION.
PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE ALGORITHMS.

 DIGITAL TWINS.
RATHER THAN STORING EVERY RAW MEASUREMENT FOREVER, THESE SYSTEMS
OFTEN RETAIN SUMMARIES, TRENDS, ANOMALIES, AND STATE ESTIMATES THAT
ARE MOST USEFUL FOR FUTURE OPERATION.

17.9 LEARNING AS COMPRESSION
LEARNING MAY ALSO BE VIEWED AS A FORM OF COMPRESSION.
A STUDENT DOES NOT MEMORIZE EVERY PAGE EVER READ.
INSTEAD,
CONCEPTS BECOME ORGANIZED INTO INCREASINGLY EFFICIENT MENTAL
STRUCTURES.
MACHINE-LEARNING MODELS SIMILARLY ADJUST PARAMETERS THAT
SUMMARIZE PATTERNS EXTRACTED FROM TRAINING DATA.
DIFFERENT LEARNING SYSTEMS EMPLOY DIFFERENT MECHANISMS, BUT EACH
TRANSFORMS EXPERIENCE INTO MORE COMPACT REPRESENTATIONS.

17.10 COMPRESSION AND GENERALIZATION
COMPRESSION IS CLOSELY RELATED TO GENERALIZATION.

 A USEFUL SCIENTIFIC THEORY APPLIES TO MANY SITUATIONS.
A USEFUL ENGINEERING DESIGN FUNCTIONS UNDER MANY OPERATING
CONDITIONS.
A USEFUL MATHEMATICAL THEOREM DESCRIBES INFINITELY MANY CASES
THROUGH A FINITE PROOF.
GENERALIZATION OFTEN DEPENDS ON IDENTIFYING REGULARITIES THAT PERMIT
CONCISE REPRESENTATION.

17.11 LIMITS OF COMPRESSION
COMPRESSION ALWAYS INVOLVES TRADE-OFFS.
TOO LITTLE COMPRESSION PRESERVES UNNECESSARY DETAIL.
TOO MUCH COMPRESSION MAY DISCARD INFORMATION ESSENTIAL FOR LATER
USE.
THE CHALLENGE IS TO PRESERVE THE INFORMATION REQUIRED FOR THE
INTENDED TASK WHILE AVOIDING UNNECESSARY COMPLEXITY.
THIS BALANCE DIFFERS ACROSS DISCIPLINES AND APPLICATIONS.

17.13 COMPRESSION AND CONTINUITY
COMPRESSION DOES NOT ELIMINATE HISTORY.
IT REORGANIZES HISTORY.
THE PRESENT CARRIES TRACES OF THE PAST,
NOT AS A COMPLETE ARCHIVE,

 BUT AS STRUCTURED CONSEQUENCES THAT CONTINUE TO INFLUENCE FUTURE

THIS IDEA PROVIDES ONE MOTIVATION FOR STUDYING PERSISTENCE ACROSS

EXACTLY HOW COMPRESSION OCCURS, HOWEVER, REMAINS SPECIFIC TO EACH

17.14 LOOKING FORWARD
COMPRESSION EXPLAINS HOW HISTORY BECOMES MANAGEABLE.

CHAPTER 18

 PERSISTENCE INVARIANTS
“EVERYTHING CHANGES. YET NOT EVERYTHING CHANGES EQUALLY. THE SEARCH

18.1 WHAT SURVIVES?
A RIVER CHANGES EVERY MOMENT.
ITS WATER FLOWS CONTINUOUSLY.
ITS SEDIMENT SHIFTS.
ITS BANKS ERODE.
YET WE CONTINUE TO IDENTIFY THE RIVER.
WHY?
BECAUSE CERTAIN ASPECTS REMAIN SUFFICIENTLY STABLE DESPITE CONTINUAL
CHANGE.
MATHEMATICS CALLS THESE ENDURING PROPERTIES INVARIANTS.
AN INVARIANT IS NOT SOMETHING THAT NEVER CHANGES.
IT IS SOMETHING THAT REMAINS UNCHANGED UNDER A SPECIFIED CLASS OF
TRANSFORMATIONS.

 THE PHRASE UNDER A SPECIFIED CLASS OF TRANSFORMATIONS IS ESSENTIAL.
EVERY INVARIANT DEPENDS ON CLEARLY STATED ASSUMPTIONS.

18.2 DEFINING AN INVARIANT
SUPPOSE A TRANSFORMATION
T:S\RIGHTARROW S'
ACTS ON A SYSTEM.
A QUANTITY
I(S)
IS CALLED AN INVARIANT IF
I(S)=I(T(S))
FOR EVERY TRANSFORMATION IN THE CLASS BEING CONSIDERED.
DIFFERENT TRANSFORMATIONS PRESERVE DIFFERENT INVARIANTS.
THERE IS NO UNIVERSAL INVARIANT FOR ALL SYSTEMS.

18.3 SIMPLE EXAMPLES
GEOMETRY PROVIDES FAMILIAR EXAMPLES.

 THE DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS REMAINS UNCHANGED UNDER RIGID
TRANSLATION.
THE ANGLES OF A TRIANGLE REMAIN UNCHANGED UNDER UNIFORM SCALING.
THE TOPOLOGY OF A COFFEE MUG AND A TORUS REMAINS EQUIVALENT UNDER
CONTINUOUS DEFORMATION.
THESE EXAMPLES ILLUSTRATE AN IMPORTANT PRINCIPLE:
THE TRANSFORMATION DETERMINES WHAT MAY REMAIN INVARIANT.

MOMENTUM.
ANGULAR MOMENTUM.
ELECTRIC CHARGE.
QUANTUM NUMBERS IN SPECIFIC SYSTEMS.
EACH CONSERVATION LAW DEPENDS UPON CLEARLY SPECIFIED CONDITIONS.
WHEN THOSE CONDITIONS CHANGE,

  THE CONSERVED QUANTITY MAY NO LONGER REMAIN INVARIANT.

VERSION IDENTIFIERS.
ALTHOUGH THE STORAGE MEDIUM CHANGES,
THE INFORMATIONAL RELATIONSHIP MAY REMAIN UNCHANGED.

 COORDINATE FRAMES.

THESE INVARIANT QUANTITIES PROVIDE RELIABLE REFERENCE POINTS FOR

 UNDERSTANDING WHICH CHARACTERISTICS REMAIN SUFFICIENTLY STABLE IS

THESE INVARIANTS HELP ENSURE RELIABLE COMPUTATION DESPITE REPEATED

ATTRACTORS.

 THESE STRUCTURES ORGANIZE LONG-TERM SYSTEM BEHAVIOR AND HELP

DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS DESCRIBE:
MOTION,
HEAT FLOW,
POPULATION DYNAMICS,
ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS,

 FLUID MECHANICS.
THESE SIMILARITIES MAKE MATHEMATICS A POWERFUL TOOL FOR
TRANSFERRING METHODS BETWEEN FIELDS.

19.4 ANALOGY IS NOT IDENTITY
FINDING THE SAME MATHEMATICS IN TWO DISCIPLINES DOES NOT MEAN THE
UNDERLYING SYSTEMS ARE PHYSICALLY IDENTICAL.
FOR EXAMPLE:
A SPRING AND AN ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT CAN BOTH SATISFY MATHEMATICALLY
SIMILAR DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS.
THIS SIMILARITY ALLOWS TECHNIQUES TO TRANSFER BETWEEN MECHANICS
AND ELECTRONICS.
IT DOES NOT IMPLY THAT SPRINGS ARE ELECTRICAL DEVICES OR CIRCUITS ARE
MECHANICAL OBJECTS.
THE MATHEMATICS IS SHARED.
THE MECHANISMS REMAIN DISTINCT.
RECOGNIZING THIS DISTINCTION IS ESSENTIAL FOR RESPONSIBLE SCIENTIFIC
REASONING.

 19.5 MODELS AND REALITY
A MATHEMATICAL MODEL IS A REPRESENTATION.
IT CAPTURES SELECTED ASPECTS OF A SYSTEM WHILE OMITTING OTHERS.
EVERY MODEL THEREFORE HAS A DOMAIN OF VALIDITY.
QUESTIONS TO ASK INCLUDE:
WHICH ASSUMPTIONS DEFINE THE MODEL?
WHICH VARIABLES ARE REPRESENTED?
WHICH EFFECTS ARE NEGLECTED?
UNDER WHAT CONDITIONS HAS THE MODEL BEEN TESTED?
THESE QUESTIONS HELP DETERMINE WHETHER A MATHEMATICAL FRAMEWORK
IS APPROPRIATE FOR A GIVEN APPLICATION.

19.6 TRANSFER OF METHODS
ALTHOUGH MECHANISMS DIFFER, MATHEMATICAL TECHNIQUES OFTEN
TRANSFER SUCCESSFULLY.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:

 OPTIMIZATION METHODS DEVELOPED FOR ENGINEERING LATER APPLIED TO
MACHINE LEARNING.
GRAPH ALGORITHMS APPLIED TO BIOLOGY.
SIGNAL-PROCESSING METHODS USED IN ASTRONOMY.
CONTROL THEORY ADAPTED FOR ROBOTICS.
STATISTICAL METHODS APPLIED ACROSS MEDICINE, ECONOMICS, AND
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE.
CROSS-DISCIPLINARY BORROWING HAS BECOME ONE OF THE ENGINES OF
MODERN SCIENTIFIC PROGRESS.

19.7 LIMITS OF TRANSFER
NOT EVERY SUCCESSFUL ANALOGY SURVIVES CAREFUL EXAMINATION.
A MATHEMATICAL SIMILARITY MAY FAIL BECAUSE:
ASSUMPTIONS DIFFER,
SCALES DIFFER,
MECHANISMS DIFFER,
MEASUREMENTS DIFFER,
BOUNDARY CONDITIONS DIFFER.

 RESPONSIBLE RESEARCH THEREFORE REQUIRES VERIFYING TRANSFERRED
IDEAS WITHIN THE TARGET DISCIPLINE RATHER THAN ASSUMING THAT
MATHEMATICAL RESEMBLANCE ALONE GUARANTEES CORRECTNESS.

19.8 MULTIPLE VALID DESCRIPTIONS
A SINGLE SYSTEM MAY ADMIT MANY USEFUL MATHEMATICAL DESCRIPTIONS.
FOR EXAMPLE, AN AIRCRAFT MAY BE ANALYZED USING:
GEOMETRY,
STRUCTURAL MECHANICS,
FLUID DYNAMICS,
CONTROL THEORY,
OPTIMIZATION,
PROBABILITY,
COMPUTATION.
EACH PERSPECTIVE ANSWERS DIFFERENT QUESTIONS.
NO SINGLE DESCRIPTION REPLACES THE OTHERS.
SCIENTIFIC UNDERSTANDING OFTEN EMERGES BY COMBINING
COMPLEMENTARY MODELS.

 19.9 INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH
MANY IMPORTANT DISCOVERIES OCCUR AT THE BOUNDARIES BETWEEN
DISCIPLINES.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
BIOINFORMATICS,
COMPUTATIONAL NEUROSCIENCE,
SYSTEMS BIOLOGY,
QUANTUM INFORMATION,
NETWORK SCIENCE,
MATERIALS ENGINEERING.
INTERDISCIPLINARY WORK SUCCEEDS WHEN MATHEMATICAL TOOLS ARE
TRANSFERRED CAREFULLY, ASSUMPTIONS ARE MADE EXPLICIT, AND EMPIRICAL
VALIDATION FOLLOWS.

19.10 EVIDENCE REMAINS ESSENTIAL
SHARED MATHEMATICS CAN MOTIVATE HYPOTHESES.
IT CANNOT BY ITSELF ESTABLISH EMPIRICAL TRUTH.

 FOR EVERY PROPOSED APPLICATION, RESEARCHERS SHOULD ASK:
WHAT OBSERVATIONS SUPPORT THIS INTERPRETATION?
WHAT PREDICTIONS DISTINGUISH IT FROM ALTERNATIVES?
WHAT EXPERIMENTS COULD FALSIFY IT?
WHAT MEASUREMENTS WOULD STRENGTHEN CONFIDENCE?
THESE QUESTIONS HELP ENSURE THAT MATHEMATICAL ELEGANCE REMAINS
CONNECTED TO EMPIRICAL SCIENCE.

19.11 A FRAMEWORK FOR COMPARISON
WHEN COMPARING IDEAS ACROSS FIELDS, THE FOLLOWING CHECKLIST IS
USEFUL:
IDENTIFY THE MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURE.
STATE THE ASSUMPTIONS.
SPECIFY THE VARIABLES.
DESCRIBE THE MECHANISM.
DEFINE THE DOMAIN OF VALIDITY.
IDENTIFY TESTABLE PREDICTIONS.
COMPARE WITH OBSERVATIONS.

 FOLLOWING THIS PROCESS REDUCES THE RISK OF DRAWING CONCLUSIONS
THAT EXTEND BEYOND WHAT THE MATHEMATICS AND EVIDENCE SUPPORT.

19.12 WHY DOMAIN INDEPENDENCE MATTERS
THE STRENGTH OF MATHEMATICS LIES IN ITS ABILITY TO DESCRIBE PATTERNS
THAT RECUR ACROSS MANY DISCIPLINES.
THE STRENGTH OF SCIENCE LIES IN ITS INSISTENCE THAT THOSE PATTERNS BE
INTERPRETED WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF APPROPRIATE EVIDENCE.
TOGETHER, MATHEMATICS AND EMPIRICAL INVESTIGATION PROVIDE
COMPLEMENTARY PATHS TOWARD UNDERSTANDING.

CHAPTER SUMMARY
DOMAIN INDEPENDENCE REFERS TO THE ABILITY OF MATHEMATICAL
STRUCTURES TO DESCRIBE MANY DIFFERENT KINDS OF SYSTEMS.
THIS FLEXIBILITY IS ONE OF MATHEMATICS’ GREATEST STRENGTHS.
AT THE SAME TIME, TRANSFERRING MATHEMATICAL IDEAS ACROSS DISCIPLINES
REQUIRES CAREFUL ATTENTION TO ASSUMPTIONS, MECHANISMS, EVIDENCE,
AND VALIDATION.

 RECOGNIZING BOTH THE POWER AND THE LIMITS OF MATHEMATICAL ANALOGY
HELPS BUILD MODELS THAT ARE BOTH ELEGANT AND SCIENTIFICALLY
RESPONSIBLE.

CHAPTER 20
FAILURE, REVISION, AND SCIENTIFIC PROGRESS

 “A THEORY IS NOT MEASURED BY HOW CONFIDENTLY IT IS STATED, BUT BY HOW
RIGOROUSLY IT SURVIVES COMPARISON WITH EVIDENCE.”

20.1 THE NATURE OF SCIENTIFIC PROGRESS
EVERY SCIENTIFIC THEORY IS PROVISIONAL.
THIS STATEMENT IS SOMETIMES MISUNDERSTOOD.
PROVISIONAL DOES NOT MEAN ARBITRARY.
IT MEANS THAT SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE REMAINS OPEN TO REFINEMENT WHEN
NEW EVIDENCE APPEARS.
THIS WILLINGNESS TO REVISE DISTINGUISHES SCIENCE FROM SYSTEMS THAT
DEPEND SOLELY ON AUTHORITY.
MATHEMATICS DEMONSTRATES LOGICAL CONSEQUENCES FROM STATED
ASSUMPTIONS.
SCIENCE ASKS WHETHER THOSE ASSUMPTIONS ADEQUATELY DESCRIBE THE
NATURAL WORLD.

20.2 FAILURE IS INFORMATION
WHEN A PREDICTION DISAGREES WITH OBSERVATION,

 SOMETHING VALUABLE HAS BEEN LEARNED.
POSSIBLE EXPLANATIONS INCLUDE:
AN INCORRECT ASSUMPTION,
AN INCOMPLETE MODEL,
MEASUREMENT ERROR,
COMPUTATIONAL ERROR,
PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN PHENOMENA.
RATHER THAN VIEWING FAILURE AS DEFEAT,
SCIENCE TREATS IT AS INFORMATION.
EACH DISCREPANCY NARROWS THE SPACE OF VIABLE EXPLANATIONS.

20.3 MODELS HAVE DOMAINS
EVERY SUCCESSFUL MODEL HAS BOUNDARIES.
NEWTONIAN MECHANICS DESCRIBES MANY ENGINEERING SYSTEMS WITH
EXTRAORDINARY ACCURACY.
GENERAL RELATIVITY BECOMES IMPORTANT UNDER DIFFERENT CONDITIONS.
FLUID MODELS DESCRIBE WATER WELL AT ONE SCALE.
MOLECULAR DESCRIPTIONS BECOME NECESSARY AT ANOTHER.

 RECOGNIZING A MODEL’S DOMAIN OF VALIDITY IS ONE OF THE MARKS OF
SCIENTIFIC MATURITY.

20.4 FALSIFIABILITY
A USEFUL SCIENTIFIC CLAIM SHOULD PERMIT MEANINGFUL COMPARISON
WITH OBSERVATION.
DIFFERENT SCIENTIFIC TRADITIONS EXPRESS THIS PRINCIPLE IN DIFFERENT
WAYS, BUT THE CENTRAL IDEA IS SIMILAR:
A CLAIM GAINS SCIENTIFIC VALUE WHEN THERE EXISTS A CONCEIVABLE
OBSERVATION OR EXPERIMENT THAT COULD SHOW THE MODEL REQUIRES
REVISION.
FALSIFIABILITY DOES NOT GUARANTEE CORRECTNESS.
IT ENSURES THAT A THEORY REMAINS ACCOUNTABLE TO EVIDENCE.

20.5 REPLICATION
ONE SUCCESSFUL EXPERIMENT IS RARELY SUFFICIENT.
INDEPENDENT REPLICATION PROVIDES CONFIDENCE THAT RESULTS ARE NOT
ARTIFACTS OF CHANCE, INSTRUMENTATION, OR ANALYSIS.

 REPLICATION MAY INVOLVE:
REPEATING MEASUREMENTS,
INDEPENDENT SOFTWARE IMPLEMENTATIONS,
ALTERNATIVE MATHEMATICAL DERIVATIONS,
DIFFERENT LABORATORIES,
DIFFERENT EXPERIMENTAL CONDITIONS.
AGREEMENT ACROSS INDEPENDENT METHODS STRENGTHENS CONFIDENCE IN
A RESULT.

20.6 UNCERTAINTY
EVERY SCIENTIFIC MEASUREMENT CONTAINS UNCERTAINTY.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
INSTRUMENT PRECISION.
ENVIRONMENTAL VARIATION.
NUMERICAL APPROXIMATION.
STATISTICAL SAMPLING.
MODEL ASSUMPTIONS.
REPORTING UNCERTAINTY IS NOT A WEAKNESS.

 IT PROVIDES READERS WITH THE INFORMATION NEEDED TO INTERPRET RESULTS
RESPONSIBLY.

20.7 REVISION
SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE GROWS THROUGH REVISION.
DEFINITIONS BECOME CLEARER.
NOTATION IMPROVES.
EXPERIMENTS BECOME MORE PRECISE.
COMPUTATIONAL METHODS ADVANCE.
EARLIER IDEAS ARE REFINED RATHER THAN SIMPLY DISCARDED.
MANY ENDURING THEORIES HAVE UNDERGONE SUBSTANTIAL REVISION WHILE
PRESERVING THEIR CENTRAL INSIGHTS.

20.8 MATHEMATICS AND EVIDENCE
MATHEMATICS AND SCIENCE PLAY COMPLEMENTARY ROLES.
MATHEMATICS ASKS:
WHAT FOLLOWS FROM THESE ASSUMPTIONS?
SCIENCE ASKS:

 DO THESE ASSUMPTIONS ADEQUATELY DESCRIBE OBSERVATIONS?
A MATHEMATICALLY CORRECT DERIVATION DOES NOT BY ITSELF ESTABLISH
EMPIRICAL TRUTH.
LIKEWISE, EXPERIMENTAL AGREEMENT WITHOUT CLEAR MATHEMATICAL
REASONING MAY LEAVE IMPORTANT QUESTIONS UNRESOLVED.
PROGRESS OFTEN REQUIRES BOTH.

20.9 RESPONSIBLE GENERALIZATION
WHEN EXTENDING A FRAMEWORK TO A NEW DOMAIN, SEVERAL QUESTIONS
SHOULD BE ASKED.
WHICH ASSUMPTIONS REMAIN VALID?
WHICH MECHANISMS DIFFER?
WHICH PREDICTIONS ARE NEW?
WHICH OBSERVATIONS COULD DISTINGUISH COMPETING EXPLANATIONS?
WHAT INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE EXISTS?
CAREFUL GENERALIZATION STRENGTHENS SCIENTIFIC WORK.
UNEXAMINED GENERALIZATION WEAKENS IT.

 20.10 THE RESEARCH CYCLE
SCIENTIFIC INVESTIGATION IS ITERATIVE.
OBSERVE.
DESCRIBE.
MODEL.
PREDICT.
MEASURE.
COMPARE.
REVISE.
REPEAT.
EACH CYCLE IMPROVES UNDERSTANDING WHILE REVEALING NEW QUESTIONS.
KNOWLEDGE GROWS THROUGH CONTINUAL REFINEMENT RATHER THAN FINAL
CERTAINTY.

20.11 INTELLECTUAL HUMILITY
THE HISTORY OF SCIENCE CONTAINS MANY EXAMPLES IN WHICH WIDELY
ACCEPTED IDEAS WERE LATER REFINED.
IMPROVED INSTRUMENTS.

 BETTER MATHEMATICS.
NEW EXPERIMENTS.
UNEXPECTED OBSERVATIONS.
PROGRESS DEPENDED NOT ON CERTAINTY,
BUT ON THE WILLINGNESS TO COMPARE IDEAS WITH EVIDENCE AND REVISE
THEM WHEN APPROPRIATE.
INTELLECTUAL HUMILITY IS THEREFORE COMPATIBLE WITH AMBITIOUS
RESEARCH.
IT ENCOURAGES CAREFUL DISTINCTION BETWEEN:
ESTABLISHED RESULTS,
COMPUTATIONAL EVIDENCE,
ENGINEERING PROPOSALS,
EMPIRICAL OBSERVATIONS,
OPEN QUESTIONS.

THE FIRST TWO VOLUMES HAVE ESTABLISHED A COMMON LANGUAGE.

 GEOMETRY,
INFORMATION,

SYMMETRY,
COMPLEXITY,
EMERGENCE,

SELECTION,
INTERACTION,
RETAINED CONSEQUENCE,
FEEDBACK,
IDENTITY,
COMPRESSION,
INVARIANTS,
DOMAIN INDEPENDENCE,
SCIENTIFIC METHODOLOGY.

 THESE CONCEPTS PROVIDE A FOUNDATION FOR THE MORE FORMAL MATERIAL

SUPPORTED COMPUTATIONALLY OR EXPERIMENTALLY, AND WHAT REMAINS AN

 CHAPTER 2
AXIOMATIC SYSTEMS
“EVERY PROOF BEGINS LONG BEFORE THE FIRST THEOREM. IT BEGINS WITH THE
ASSUMPTIONS WE AGREE TO ACCEPT.”

2.1 THE FOUNDATIONS OF REASON
IMAGINE ATTEMPTING TO CONSTRUCT A CATHEDRAL.
BEFORE THE FIRST STONE IS PLACED,
CERTAIN ASSUMPTIONS ALREADY EXIST.
THE GROUND CAN SUPPORT THE WEIGHT.
THE MEASUREMENTS ARE CONSISTENT.
THE MATERIALS BEHAVE PREDICTABLY.
WITHOUT THESE ASSUMPTIONS,

 CONSTRUCTION CANNOT BEGIN.
MATHEMATICS PROCEEDS SIMILARLY.
BEFORE ANY THEOREM CAN BE PROVEN,
THERE MUST EXIST A COLLECTION OF ACCEPTED STARTING STATEMENTS.
THESE ARE CALLED AXIOMS.

2.2 WHAT IS AN AXIOM?
AN AXIOM IS A STATEMENT ACCEPTED WITHOUT PROOF WITHIN A PARTICULAR
FORMAL SYSTEM.
THIS DOES NOT MEAN THE STATEMENT IS UNIVERSALLY TRUE.
IT MEANS THAT, FOR THE PURPOSES OF DEVELOPING THAT MATHEMATICAL
SYSTEM, IT SERVES AS A STARTING POINT.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
EUCLID’S GEOMETRIC POSTULATES.
THE AXIOMS OF SET THEORY.
THE FIELD AXIOMS FOR THE REAL NUMBERS.
DIFFERENT AXIOMS PRODUCE DIFFERENT MATHEMATICAL UNIVERSES.

 2.3 DEFINITIONS VERSUS AXIOMS
DEFINITIONS AND AXIOMS SERVE DIFFERENT PURPOSES.
DEFINITIONS ESTABLISH MEANING.
EXAMPLE:
A CIRCLE IS THE SET OF ALL POINTS EQUIDISTANT FROM ONE CENTER.
NOTHING HAS BEEN CLAIMED.
ONLY VOCABULARY HAS BEEN INTRODUCED.
AN AXIOM, HOWEVER, MAKES AN ASSUMPTION.
FOR EXAMPLE,
THROUGH ANY TWO DISTINCT POINTS THERE EXISTS EXACTLY ONE STRAIGHT
LINE.
NOW MATHEMATICS HAS SOMETHING UPON WHICH REASONING MAY BEGIN.

2.4 FORMAL SYSTEMS
A FORMAL SYSTEM CONSISTS OF FOUR COMPONENTS.
SYMBOLS
THE ALPHABET OF THE SYSTEM.
FORMATION RULES

 HOW VALID EXPRESSIONS MAY BE WRITTEN.
AXIOMS
ACCEPTED STARTING STATEMENTS.
RULES OF INFERENCE
METHODS BY WHICH NEW STATEMENTS MAY BE DERIVED.
TOGETHER THESE COMPONENTS DEFINE AN ENTIRE MATHEMATICAL UNIVERSE.

2.5 CONSISTENCY
PERHAPS THE MOST IMPORTANT PROPERTY OF A FORMAL SYSTEM IS
CONSISTENCY.
A SYSTEM IS CONSISTENT IF IT CANNOT PROVE BOTH
P
AND
\NEG P.
IN OTHER WORDS,
IT NEVER PROVES A STATEMENT AND ITS CONTRADICTION.
WITHOUT CONSISTENCY,
EVERY STATEMENT BECOMES PROVABLE,

 AND MATHEMATICAL REASONING LOSES ALL MEANING.

2.6 INDEPENDENCE
SOME AXIOMS CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THE OTHERS.
THESE ARE CALLED INDEPENDENT AXIOMS.
FOR EXAMPLE,
EUCLID’S PARALLEL POSTULATE WAS EVENTUALLY SHOWN TO BE INDEPENDENT
OF HIS REMAINING AXIOMS.
REPLACING IT LED TO ENTIRELY NEW GEOMETRIES:
HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY.
ELLIPTIC GEOMETRY.
THE DISCOVERY DEMONSTRATED THAT CHANGING ONE ASSUMPTION CAN
RESHAPE AN ENTIRE MATHEMATICAL LANDSCAPE.

2.7 COMPLETENESS
A FORMAL SYSTEM IS CALLED COMPLETE IF EVERY STATEMENT EXPRESSIBLE
WITHIN THE SYSTEM CAN BE PROVEN TRUE OR FALSE FROM ITS AXIOMS.
THIS IDEA IS SUBTLE.

 IN THE TWENTIETH CENTURY,
KURT GÖDEL DEMONSTRATED PROFOUND LIMITATIONS ON COMPLETENESS
FOR SUFFICIENTLY EXPRESSIVE FORMAL SYSTEMS.
HIS INCOMPLETENESS THEOREMS SHOWED THAT CERTAIN TRUE STATEMENTS
CANNOT BE PROVEN WITHIN THE SYSTEM ITSELF UNDER APPROPRIATE
ASSUMPTIONS.
THESE RESULTS TRANSFORMED MODERN MATHEMATICAL LOGIC.

2.8 MINIMAL ASSUMPTIONS
STRONG THEORIES OFTEN BEGIN FROM SURPRISINGLY SMALL COLLECTIONS OF
ASSUMPTIONS.
THIS PRINCIPLE APPEARS THROUGHOUT MATHEMATICS.
A FEW AXIOMS GENERATE:
ARITHMETIC.
ALGEBRA.
GEOMETRY.
TOPOLOGY.
ANALYSIS.

 GROUP THEORY.
THE POWER LIES NOT IN THE NUMBER OF ASSUMPTIONS,
BUT IN WHAT FOLLOWS FROM THEM.

2.9 CONSTRUCTING MATHEMATICAL WORLDS
DIFFERENT AXIOM SYSTEMS PRODUCE DIFFERENT MATHEMATICAL
STRUCTURES.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
EUCLIDEAN GEOMETRY.
NON-EUCLIDEAN GEOMETRY.
CLASSICAL LOGIC.
INTUITIONISTIC LOGIC.
SET THEORY.
CATEGORY THEORY.
EACH FRAMEWORK IS INTERNALLY CONSISTENT ACCORDING TO ITS OWN
ASSUMPTIONS.
THE QUESTION IS NOT
“WHICH IS ABSOLUTELY CORRECT?”

 BUT RATHER
“FOR WHICH PROBLEMS IS THIS FRAMEWORK APPROPRIATE?”

2.10 HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS
MANY ERRORS IN REASONING ARISE FROM ASSUMPTIONS THAT REMAIN
UNSTATED.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
ASSUMING CONTINUITY.
ASSUMING DIFFERENTIABILITY.
ASSUMING FINITE DIMENSION.
ASSUMING INDEPENDENCE.
ASSUMING SYMMETRY.
FORMAL MATHEMATICS ENCOURAGES EVERY IMPORTANT ASSUMPTION TO BE
MADE EXPLICIT.
DOING SO IMPROVES CLARITY AND ALLOWS OTHERS TO EVALUATE THE
ARGUMENT OBJECTIVELY.

2.11 SCIENTIFIC MODELS

 SCIENTIFIC THEORIES ALSO BEGIN WITH ASSUMPTIONS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
IDEAL GASES.
RIGID BODIES.
PERFECT FLUIDS.
FRICTIONLESS SURFACES.
POINT PARTICLES.
THESE ASSUMPTIONS ARE OFTEN APPROXIMATIONS RATHER THAN EXACT
DESCRIPTIONS OF REALITY.
THEIR USEFULNESS DEPENDS UPON HOW ACCURATELY THEY MODEL THE
PHENOMENA UNDER INVESTIGATION.
MATHEMATICS PROVIDES THE LOGICAL CONSEQUENCES.
EXPERIMENT DETERMINES WHETHER THE ASSUMPTIONS ARE APPROPRIATE.

2.12 DESIGNING NEW FRAMEWORKS
WHENEVER RESEARCHERS PROPOSE A NEW MATHEMATICAL FRAMEWORK,
A DISCIPLINED SEQUENCE IS HELPFUL:
DEFINE THE OBJECTS.

 DEFINE THE SYMBOLS.
STATE EVERY AXIOM EXPLICITLY.
SPECIFY RULES OF INFERENCE.
DERIVE PROPOSITIONS.
PROVE LEMMAS.
ESTABLISH THEOREMS.
COMPARE PREDICTIONS WITH EXISTING MATHEMATICS OR EMPIRICAL
EVIDENCE WHERE APPLICABLE.
FOLLOWING THIS PROGRESSION HELPS DISTINGUISH FOUNDATIONAL
ASSUMPTIONS FROM DERIVED RESULTS.

2.13 WHY FOUNDATIONS MATTER
THE GREATEST MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURES EVER BUILT—
CALCULUS,
LINEAR ALGEBRA,
TOPOLOGY,
FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS,
MODERN GEOMETRY—

 ALL REST UPON CAREFULLY CHOSEN AXIOMS.
WEAK FOUNDATIONS PRODUCE FRAGILE THEORIES.
STRONG FOUNDATIONS SUPPORT CENTURIES OF FURTHER DEVELOPMENT.

CHAPTER 3
PROPOSITIONS, LEMMAS, AND THEOREMS

 “GREAT MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURES ARE NOT BUILT IN A SINGLE LEAP. THEY
RISE ONE CAREFULLY JUSTIFIED STATEMENT AT A TIME.”

3.1 BUILDING MATHEMATICS
A COMPLETED MATHEMATICAL THEORY OFTEN APPEARS ELEGANT AND
INEVITABLE.
YET EVERY THEOREM BEGAN AS A SEQUENCE OF SMALL OBSERVATIONS.
DEFINITIONS ESTABLISHED THE LANGUAGE.
AXIOMS ESTABLISHED THE ASSUMPTIONS.
NOW REASONING BEGINS.
THE PURPOSE OF FORMAL MATHEMATICS IS NOT MERELY TO REACH
CONCLUSIONS, BUT TO DEMONSTRATE WHY THOSE CONCLUSIONS
NECESSARILY FOLLOW FROM THE ADOPTED ASSUMPTIONS.

3.2 MATHEMATICAL STATEMENTS
EVERY MATHEMATICAL ARGUMENT CONSISTS OF STATEMENTS.
A STATEMENT MUST POSSESS A DEFINITE TRUTH VALUE WITHIN THE ADOPTED
FORMAL SYSTEM.

 EXAMPLES INCLUDE
2+2=4,
7 \TEXT{ IS PRIME},
A\SUBSETEQ B.
QUESTIONS,
COMMANDS,
OR UNDEFINED EXPRESSIONS ARE NOT MATHEMATICAL STATEMENTS.
ONLY STATEMENTS MAY APPEAR WITHIN FORMAL PROOFS.

3.3 PROPOSITIONS
A PROPOSITION IS A MATHEMATICAL STATEMENT WHOSE PROOF IS USEFUL BUT
WHOSE IMPORTANCE IS RELATIVELY LOCAL.
PROPOSITIONS OFTEN ESTABLISH PRELIMINARY PROPERTIES THAT PREPARE
LARGER ARGUMENTS.
EXAMPLE.
SUPPOSE
A\SUBSETEQ B
AND

 B\SUBSETEQ C.
THEN
A\SUBSETEQ C.
ALTHOUGH SIMPLE,
SUCH PROPOSITIONS BECOME ESSENTIAL BUILDING BLOCKS.

3.4 LEMMAS
A LEMMA IS AN INTERMEDIATE THEOREM PROVED PRIMARILY TO SUPPORT
ANOTHER RESULT.
THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN A PROPOSITION AND A LEMMA IS PRACTICAL
RATHER THAN ABSOLUTE.
SOME OF HISTORY’S MOST FAMOUS LEMMAS LATER BECAME CELEBRATED
RESULTS IN THEIR OWN RIGHT.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
ZORN’S LEMMA
SCHWARZ LEMMA
URYSOHN’S LEMMA

 A LEMMA OFTEN SOLVES ONE DIFFICULT OBSTACLE THAT REPEATEDLY APPEARS
THROUGHOUT A THEORY.

3.5 THEOREMS
A THEOREM IS A MATHEMATICALLY SIGNIFICANT STATEMENT ESTABLISHED
THROUGH RIGOROUS PROOF.
THE IMPORTANCE OF A THEOREM DEPENDS UPON ITS USEFULNESS,
ITS DEPTH,
ITS GENERALITY,
OR ITS EXPLANATORY POWER.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
THE FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF ALGEBRA.
THE SPECTRAL THEOREM.
THE HAHN–BANACH THEOREM.
THE CENTRAL LIMIT THEOREM.
A THEOREM IS NEVER ACCEPTED BECAUSE IT APPEARS PLAUSIBLE.
ITS ACCEPTANCE DEPENDS ENTIRELY UPON THE VALIDITY OF ITS PROOF.

 3.6 COROLLARIES
SOME CONCLUSIONS FOLLOW ALMOST IMMEDIATELY FROM AN ESTABLISHED
THEOREM.
THESE ARE CALLED COROLLARIES.
EXAMPLE.
IF A THEOREM PROVES EVERY INVERTIBLE MATRIX HAS NONZERO
DETERMINANT,
THEN A COROLLARY STATES
MATRICES WITH DETERMINANT ZERO ARE NOT INVERTIBLE.
NO SUBSTANTIAL NEW ARGUMENT IS REQUIRED.

8.1 FROM CONTINUOUS MATHEMATICS TO COMPUTATION
MANY MATHEMATICAL MODELS DESCRIBE CONTINUOUS EVOLUTION.
COMPUTERS, HOWEVER, OPERATE THROUGH DISCRETE COMPUTATIONS.
NUMERICAL ANALYSIS PROVIDES THE MATHEMATICAL BRIDGE BETWEEN EXACT
EQUATIONS AND FINITE COMPUTATION.
RATHER THAN REPLACING MATHEMATICS,
NUMERICAL METHODS APPROXIMATE MATHEMATICAL SOLUTIONS WHILE
PROVIDING TOOLS FOR ANALYZING APPROXIMATION ERROR, STABILITY, AND
CONVERGENCE.

8.5 IMPROVED EULER (HEUN’S METHOD)
A MORE ACCURATE SECOND-ORDER METHOD COMPUTES AN INTERMEDIATE

CONCEPTUALLY,

AVERAGE THE TWO SLOPES.
THIS OFTEN REDUCES NUMERICAL ERROR WHILE REMAINING
COMPUTATIONALLY EFFICIENT.

8.6 RUNGE–KUTTA METHODS
HIGHER-ORDER RUNGE–KUTTA METHODS EVALUATE MULTIPLE INTERMEDIATE
SLOPES WITHIN EACH TIMESTEP.
THE CLASSICAL FOURTH-ORDER RUNGE–KUTTA (RK4) METHOD IS WIDELY USED
BECAUSE IT PROVIDES AN EXCELLENT BALANCE BETWEEN ACCURACY AND
COMPUTATIONAL EFFORT FOR MANY PROBLEMS.
THE CHOICE OF INTEGRATION METHOD SHOULD REFLECT THE PROPERTIES OF
THE UNDERLYING SYSTEM.

8.7 ADAPTIVE STEP SIZE

ADAPTIVE METHODS ESTIMATE LOCAL ERROR AND ADJUST

 AUTOMATICALLY.
WHEN DYNAMICS CHANGE RAPIDLY,
SMALLER STEPS IMPROVE ACCURACY.
WHEN EVOLUTION IS SMOOTH,
LARGER STEPS IMPROVE EFFICIENCY.
ADAPTIVE INTEGRATION IS ESPECIALLY VALUABLE FOR SYSTEMS EXHIBITING
MULTIPLE TIME SCALES.

8.8 STABILITY OF NUMERICAL SCHEMES
A NUMERICAL METHOD SHOULD NOT INTRODUCE BEHAVIOR ABSENT FROM
THE MATHEMATICAL MODEL.
STABILITY ANALYSIS STUDIES WHETHER NUMERICAL ERRORS REMAIN
CONTROLLED DURING REPEATED COMPUTATION.
AN UNSTABLE NUMERICAL SCHEME MAY DIVERGE EVEN WHEN THE
UNDERLYING DIFFERENTIAL EQUATION POSSESSES STABLE SOLUTIONS.
THE STABILITY REGION DEPENDS UPON BOTH THE INTEGRATION METHOD AND
THE PROBLEM BEING SOLVED.

 8.9 CONVERGENCE
A NUMERICAL METHOD IS CONVERGENT IF ITS APPROXIMATION APPROACHES
THE EXACT SOLUTION AS THE TIMESTEP DECREASES.
CONSISTENCY AND STABILITY TOGETHER OFTEN IMPLY CONVERGENCE UNDER
APPROPRIATE ASSUMPTIONS, A RELATIONSHIP FORMALIZED BY CLASSICAL
RESULTS SUCH AS THE LAX EQUIVALENCE THEOREM FOR SUITABLE CLASSES OF
PROBLEMS.

8.10 ERROR ANALYSIS
NUMERICAL ERROR GENERALLY CONSISTS OF SEVERAL COMPONENTS.
LOCAL TRUNCATION ERROR
THE ERROR INTRODUCED DURING ONE TIMESTEP.
GLOBAL ERROR
THE ACCUMULATED ERROR ACROSS MANY TIMESTEPS.
ROUND-OFF ERROR
FINITE-PRECISION ARITHMETIC PERFORMED BY DIGITAL COMPUTERS.
UNDERSTANDING THESE SOURCES HELPS GUIDE THE SELECTION OF
ALGORITHMS AND STEP SIZES.

 8.11 STIFF SYSTEMS
SOME SYSTEMS CONTAIN BOTH VERY FAST AND VERY SLOW DYNAMICS.
SUCH SYSTEMS ARE CALLED STIFF.
EXPLICIT METHODS MAY REQUIRE EXTREMELY SMALL TIMESTEPS TO REMAIN
STABLE.
IMPLICIT METHODS OFTEN PROVIDE BETTER STABILITY FOR STIFF PROBLEMS,
THOUGH AT INCREASED COMPUTATIONAL COST.
THE CHOICE BETWEEN EXPLICIT AND IMPLICIT METHODS DEPENDS UPON THE
MATHEMATICAL PROPERTIES OF THE MODEL.

SPARSE MATRIX ALGORITHMS.

9.2 COMPUTATIONAL MODELS
A COMPUTATIONAL MODEL CONSISTS OF:

 MATHEMATICAL EQUATIONS,
NUMERICAL ALGORITHMS,
INITIAL CONDITIONS,
BOUNDARY CONDITIONS,
IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS.
EACH COMPONENT INFLUENCES THE RESULTING SIMULATION.
CAREFUL DOCUMENTATION OF ASSUMPTIONS AND ALGORITHMS IS ESSENTIAL

9.3 HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTING
MANY SCIENTIFIC PROBLEMS EXCEED THE CAPABILITIES OF A SINGLE

HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTING (HPC) DISTRIBUTES WORK ACROSS

REPRESENTATIVE ARCHITECTURES INCLUDE:
MULTICORE PROCESSORS,
GRAPHICS PROCESSING UNITS (GPUS),
DISTRIBUTED-MEMORY CLUSTERS,

 CLOUD COMPUTING ENVIRONMENTS.

 BIOLOGICAL ECOSYSTEMS.
EACH SUBSYSTEM MAY BE SIMULATED INDEPENDENTLY WHILE EXCHANGING

DISTRIBUTED SIMULATION MIRRORS THE MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURE OF

9.7 UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION

SOURCES OF UNCERTAINTY INCLUDE:
MEASUREMENT ERROR,
PARAMETER UNCERTAINTY,
NUMERICAL APPROXIMATION,
INCOMPLETE MODELS.
UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION SEEKS TO CHARACTERIZE HOW THESE
UNCERTAINTIES INFLUENCE SIMULATION OUTCOMES.
METHODS INCLUDE SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS, PROBABILISTIC MODELING, AND
SAMPLING TECHNIQUES.

 9.8 VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION
SCIENTIFIC COMPUTING DISTINGUISHES TWO COMPLEMENTARY QUESTIONS.
VERIFICATION
“WAS THE MATHEMATICAL MODEL IMPLEMENTED CORRECTLY?”
VALIDATION
“DOES THE MODEL ADEQUATELY REPRESENT THE SYSTEM IT IS INTENDED TO
DESCRIBE FOR THE STATED PURPOSE?”
VERIFICATION CONCERNS CORRECTNESS OF IMPLEMENTATION.
VALIDATION CONCERNS AGREEMENT WITH OBSERVATIONS OR EXPERIMENTAL
EVIDENCE WHERE APPLICABLE.
BOTH ARE NECESSARY IN COMPUTATIONAL SCIENCE.

9.9 REPRODUCIBILITY

FORMAL VERIFICATION AND MACHINE-ASSISTED MATHEMATICS
“A PROOF CONVINCES THE HUMAN MIND. FORMAL VERIFICATION CONVINCES A
PRECISELY DEFINED LOGICAL SYSTEM.”

10.1 WHY FORMAL VERIFICATION?
AS MATHEMATICS GROWS IN COMPLEXITY,
SO DOES THE POSSIBILITY OF UNNOTICED ERROR.
MODERN PROOFS MAY SPAN HUNDREDS OF PAGES.
LARGE ENGINEERING SYSTEMS MAY CONTAIN MILLIONS OF LINES OF CODE.

 FORMAL VERIFICATION PROVIDES MATHEMATICAL TECHNIQUES THAT ALLOW
LOGICAL ARGUMENTS AND ALGORITHMS TO BE CHECKED AGAINST EXPLICITLY
SPECIFIED RULES.
RATHER THAN REPLACING HUMAN REASONING,
FORMAL VERIFICATION COMPLEMENTS IT BY REDUCING AMBIGUITY AND
IMPROVING CONFIDENCE IN CORRECTNESS.

10.2 FORMAL SYSTEMS
A FORMAL VERIFICATION SYSTEM BEGINS WITH:
A FORMAL LANGUAGE,
LOGICAL RULES,
AXIOMS,
INFERENCE RULES.
EVERY PROOF BECOMES A SEQUENCE OF EXPLICITLY JUSTIFIED LOGICAL STEPS.
NOTHING IS ACCEPTED MERELY BECAUSE IT APPEARS PLAUSIBLE.

10.3 PROOF ASSISTANTS

 A PROOF ASSISTANT IS SOFTWARE THAT HELPS CONSTRUCT FORMALLY VERIFIED
PROOFS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
LEAN
COQ
ISABELLE/HOL
HOL LIGHT
THESE SYSTEMS VERIFY THAT EACH LOGICAL STEP FOLLOWS FROM PREVIOUSLY
ESTABLISHED DEFINITIONS, AXIOMS, OR THEOREMS.
THEY ASSIST MATHEMATICIANS—THEY DO NOT INDEPENDENTLY INVENT
MATHEMATICAL TRUTH.

10.4 FORMAL SPECIFICATIONS
BEFORE VERIFICATION CAN BEGIN,
THE INTENDED BEHAVIOR OF A MATHEMATICAL OBJECT OR ALGORITHM MUST
BE SPECIFIED PRECISELY.
A SPECIFICATION DEFINES:
INPUTS,

 OUTPUTS,
ASSUMPTIONS,
REQUIRED PROPERTIES,
CONSTRAINTS.
A PROGRAM CANNOT BE PROVEN CORRECT WITHOUT FIRST DEFINING WHAT
“CORRECT” MEANS.

10.5 CORRECTNESS
FORMAL VERIFICATION DISTINGUISHES SEVERAL NOTIONS OF CORRECTNESS.
LOGICAL CORRECTNESS
THE PROOF FOLLOWS VALID INFERENCE RULES.

ALGORITHMIC CORRECTNESS
THE ALGORITHM SATISFIES ITS SPECIFICATION.

IMPLEMENTATION CORRECTNESS
THE SOFTWARE FAITHFULLY IMPLEMENTS THE INTENDED ALGORITHM.
EACH LEVEL ADDRESSES A DIFFERENT SOURCE OF POTENTIAL ERROR.

 10.6 SOUNDNESS
A VERIFICATION SYSTEM IS SOUND IF IT NEVER PROVES FALSE STATEMENTS
WITHIN ITS FORMAL LOGIC.
SOUNDNESS IS ONE OF THE FOUNDATIONAL REQUIREMENTS OF TRUSTWORTHY
PROOF SYSTEMS.
WITHOUT SOUNDNESS,
FORMAL VERIFICATION WOULD LOSE ITS VALUE.

10.7 COMPLETENESS
SOME LOGICAL SYSTEMS ARE COMPLETE FOR PARTICULAR CLASSES OF
STATEMENTS.
OTHERS ARE INTENTIONALLY INCOMPLETE BUT COMPUTATIONALLY PRACTICAL.
AS DISCUSSED IN EARLIER VOLUMES,
GÖDEL’S INCOMPLETENESS THEOREMS PLACE IMPORTANT LIMITS ON
SUFFICIENTLY EXPRESSIVE FORMAL SYSTEMS UNDER APPROPRIATE
ASSUMPTIONS.

 FORMAL VERIFICATION WORKS WITHIN THESE WELL-UNDERSTOOD LOGICAL
BOUNDARIES.

10.8 VERIFIED ALGORITHMS
ALGORITHMS THEMSELVES MAY BE FORMALLY VERIFIED.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
SORTING ALGORITHMS,
GRAPH ALGORITHMS,
NUMERICAL METHODS,
CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROTOCOLS,
CONTROL SOFTWARE,
COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS.
VERIFICATION DEMONSTRATES THAT THE IMPLEMENTATION SATISFIES THE
MATHEMATICAL SPECIFICATION—NOT THAT THE SPECIFICATION ITSELF
NECESSARILY MODELS REALITY.

10.9 CERTIFIED NUMERICAL COMPUTATION
NUMERICAL COMPUTATION INTRODUCES APPROXIMATION.

 FORMAL METHODS CAN SOMETIMES PROVIDE RIGOROUS ERROR BOUNDS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
INTERVAL ARITHMETIC,
CERTIFIED OPTIMIZATION,
VERIFIED INTEGRATION,
VALIDATED EIGENVALUE COMPUTATION.
THESE TECHNIQUES COMBINE NUMERICAL ANALYSIS WITH FORMAL
GUARANTEES UNDER EXPLICITLY STATED ASSUMPTIONS.

10.10 FORMAL MODELS AND PHYSICAL SYSTEMS
A FORMALLY VERIFIED MODEL IS MATHEMATICALLY CORRECT WITH RESPECT TO
ITS SPECIFICATION.
WHETHER THAT SPECIFICATION ACCURATELY REPRESENTS A PHYSICAL SYSTEM
REMAINS A SEPARATE EMPIRICAL QUESTION.
IT IS THEREFORE USEFUL TO DISTINGUISH:
MATHEMATICAL CORRECTNESS,
IMPLEMENTATION CORRECTNESS,
EMPIRICAL ADEQUACY.

 EACH REQUIRES DIFFERENT METHODS OF EVALUATION.

10.11 VERIFICATION WORKFLOWS
A DISCIPLINED VERIFICATION WORKFLOW OFTEN INCLUDES:
DEFINE MATHEMATICAL OBJECTS.
STATE ASSUMPTIONS EXPLICITLY.
SPECIFY DESIRED PROPERTIES.
CONSTRUCT PROOFS.
VERIFY COMPUTATIONAL IMPLEMENTATIONS.
TEST NUMERICAL BEHAVIOR.
COMPARE WITH EXPERIMENTAL OR OBSERVATIONAL EVIDENCE WHERE
APPLICABLE.
EACH STAGE STRENGTHENS CONFIDENCE IN DIFFERENT ASPECTS OF THE
OVERALL FRAMEWORK.

 POSSIBLE VERIFICATION TASKS INCLUDE:

SUCH VERIFICATION DOES NOT ESTABLISH NEW MATHEMATICS

10.13 MACHINE ASSISTANCE IN MODERN MATHEMATICS

EXPLORE CONJECTURES,
SEARCH FOR COUNTEREXAMPLES,
AUTOMATE ROUTINE REASONING,
CERTIFY COMPUTATIONS.

 HUMAN CREATIVITY REMAINS CENTRAL TO CHOOSING DEFINITIONS, FRAMING

MACHINE ASSISTANCE PROVIDES ADDITIONAL RIGOR AND SCALABILITY.

10.14 TOWARD INTEGRATED MATHEMATICAL SYSTEMS

PRINCIPLES OF MATHEMATICAL MODELING
“EVERY MATHEMATICAL MODEL IS A CONVERSATION BETWEEN REALITY AND
ABSTRACTION. ITS STRENGTH DEPENDS ON MAKING THAT CONVERSATION
EXPLICIT.”

19.1 WHY MATHEMATICAL MODELS EXIST
THE WORLD IS EXTRAORDINARILY COMPLEX.
NO MATHEMATICAL MODEL CAPTURES EVERY DETAIL.
INSTEAD,
MODELS ISOLATE THE FEATURES RELEVANT TO A PARTICULAR QUESTION WHILE
DELIBERATELY OMITTING OTHERS.
A USEFUL MODEL THEREFORE BALANCES:
SIMPLICITY,
EXPLANATORY POWER,
COMPUTATIONAL TRACTABILITY,
PREDICTIVE CAPABILITY WITHIN ITS INTENDED DOMAIN.

 THE QUALITY OF A MODEL DEPENDS NOT ON ITS COMPLEXITY, BUT ON HOW
WELL IT SERVES ITS STATED PURPOSE.

19.2 ABSTRACTION
ABSTRACTION REMOVES UNNECESSARY DETAIL WHILE PRESERVING ESSENTIAL
MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURE.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
REPRESENTING A PLANET AS A POINT MASS.
REPRESENTING A COMMUNICATION NETWORK AS A GRAPH.
REPRESENTING UNCERTAINTY THROUGH PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS.
REPRESENTING MOTION BY DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS.
DIFFERENT ABSTRACTIONS MAY BE APPROPRIATE FOR DIFFERENT QUESTIONS.

19.3 ASSUMPTIONS
EVERY MATHEMATICAL MODEL BEGINS WITH ASSUMPTIONS.
EXAMPLES INCLUDE:
CONTINUITY,
DIFFERENTIABILITY,

 INDEPENDENCE,
CONSERVATION,
BOUNDEDNESS,
SYMMETRY,
STATIONARITY.
ASSUMPTIONS DETERMINE BOTH THE POWER AND THE LIMITATIONS OF A
MODEL.
EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS MAKE MODELS EASIER TO UNDERSTAND, TEST, AND
REVISE.

19.4 SCOPE
EVERY MODEL HAS A DOMAIN OF APPLICABILITY.
QUESTIONS TO CONSIDER INCLUDE:
WHICH SYSTEMS DOES THE MODEL REPRESENT?
UNDER WHAT CONDITIONS?
WHICH PHENOMENA ARE INTENTIONALLY EXCLUDED?
WHICH VARIABLES ARE TREATED AS EXTERNAL INPUTS?

 A MODEL SHOULD NOT BE EXPECTED TO ANSWER QUESTIONS BEYOND ITS
INTENDED SCOPE.

19.5 PARAMETERS
MODELS OFTEN CONTAIN PARAMETERS,
\THETA.
PARAMETERS MAY BE:
MEASURED,
ESTIMATED,
CALIBRATED,
INFERRED.
PARAMETER UNCERTAINTY SHOULD BE ACKNOWLEDGED EXPLICITLY,
PARTICULARLY WHEN PREDICTIONS DEPEND SENSITIVELY UPON THEIR VALUES.

19.6 VALIDATION
VALIDATION ASKS:
DOES THE MODEL ADEQUATELY REPRESENT THE SYSTEM IT IS INTENDED TO
DESCRIBE FOR THE STATED PURPOSE?

 VALIDATION METHODS MAY INCLUDE:
COMPARISON WITH OBSERVATIONS,
EXPERIMENTAL TESTING,
BENCHMARK PROBLEMS,
CROSS-VALIDATION,
SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS.
VALIDATION IS DISTINCT FROM MATHEMATICAL PROOF.
A MATHEMATICALLY CORRECT MODEL MAY STILL FAIL TO REPRESENT A
PARTICULAR PHYSICAL SYSTEM ADEQUATELY.

19.7 VERIFICATION
VERIFICATION ASKS:
HAS THE MATHEMATICAL MODEL BEEN IMPLEMENTED CORRECTLY?
VERIFICATION CONCERNS:
EQUATIONS,
ALGORITHMS,
SOFTWARE,
NUMERICAL METHODS.

 VALIDATION CONCERNS CORRESPONDENCE WITH THE INTENDED APPLICATION.
BOTH ARE ESSENTIAL.

19.8 UNCERTAINTY
NO MODEL IS FREE FROM UNCERTAINTY.
REPRESENTATIVE SOURCES INCLUDE:
MEASUREMENT ERROR,
PARAMETER UNCERTAINTY,
NUMERICAL APPROXIMATION,
INCOMPLETE KNOWLEDGE,
STOCHASTIC VARIABILITY.
QUANTIFYING UNCERTAINTY IMPROVES INTERPRETATION AND DECISIONMAKING.

19.9 MODEL COMPARISON
MULTIPLE MATHEMATICAL MODELS MAY DESCRIBE THE SAME PHENOMENON.
USEFUL COMPARISON CRITERIA INCLUDE:
PREDICTIVE ACCURACY,

 COMPUTATIONAL EFFICIENCY,
INTERPRETABILITY,
ROBUSTNESS,
THEORETICAL CONSISTENCY,
EMPIRICAL SUPPORT WITHIN THE INTENDED DOMAIN.
DIFFERENT APPLICATIONS MAY PRIORITIZE THESE CRITERIA DIFFERENTLY.

19.10 SIMPLICITY AND COMPLEXITY
A MORE COMPLICATED MODEL IS NOT NECESSARILY A BETTER MODEL.
INCREASING COMPLEXITY MAY IMPROVE FIDELITY,
BUT CAN ALSO INTRODUCE:
OVERFITTING,
COMPUTATIONAL COST,
PARAMETER SENSITIVITY,
INTERPRETABILITY CHALLENGES.
CHOOSING AN APPROPRIATE LEVEL OF COMPLEXITY IS AN IMPORTANT
MODELING DECISION.

MODEL DEVELOPMENT IS OFTEN ITERATIVE.

EACH CYCLE IMPROVES UNDERSTANDING BY INCORPORATING NEW EVIDENCE,

RESOURCE BOUNDARY, AND SUPERVISION MODEL.

THE DISTANCE-DECAY COMPONENT IS
\PHI(D)
=
E^{-D/L}.

\BOXED{
\PHI'(D)
=
-\FRAC1L E^{-D/L}
=
-\FRAC{\PHI(D)}{L}.
}
ITS SECOND DERIVATIVE IS
\BOXED{
\PHI''(D)
=
\FRAC1{L^2}E^{-D/L}
=
\FRAC{\PHI(D)}{L^2}.
}
THUS THE KERNEL CONTRIBUTION IS:
STRICTLY DECREASING IN D;

 CONVEX IN D.
WITH RESPECT TO L,
\BOXED{
\FRAC{\PARTIAL\PHI}{\PARTIAL L}
=
\FRAC{D}{L^2}E^{-D/L}.
}
THE SECOND DERIVATIVE WITH RESPECT TO L IS
\BOXED{
\FRAC{\PARTIAL^2\PHI}{\PARTIAL L^2}
=

\LEFT(
\FRAC{D^2}{L^4}
\FRAC{2D}{L^3}
\RIGHT).
}

 EQUIVALENTLY,
\FRAC{\PARTIAL^2\PHI}{\PARTIAL L^2}
=
\FRAC{D(D-2L)}{L^4}

RECALL

\BOXED{

\BOXED{
\FRAC{\PARTIAL H_{IJ}}{\PARTIAL W_A}

BECAUSE

\BOXED{

{2D_{IJ}}
\LEFT(

\RIGHT)

 \BOXED{
